screenings.title: Fallen Angels
screenings.description: Part hard-boiled crime thriller and part soft, featherweight giddiness, Fallen Angels was first conceived as a segment of Wong’s Chungking Express, then developed into a darker companion piece to his glistening pop-romantic masterpiece, the story of a hitman (Leon Lai) looking to hang up his gun, the business partner (Michelle Reis) who quietly lusts after him, and a mute troublemaker (Takeshi Kaneshiro) running amok in Hong Kong. Christopher Doyle’s cinematography has never been more woozily, blearily beautiful, nor has the Fragrant Harbor ever been put on screen with such transfixing nocturnal glamor.

screenings.title: The Hunger
screenings.description: A lush vampire romance with sex and style to spare, much of it provided by stars Catherine Deneuve and David Bowie as a couple of posh, centuries-old nightclubbing New York bloodsuckers who, when one begins to show the first signs of aging, recruit assistance from Susan Sarandon’s geriatrics researcher, then find themselves in a very, very attractive throuple. Yes, that’s “Bela Lugosi’s Dead” artists Bauhaus in a brief cameo.

screenings.title: Der Fan
screenings.description: Teen runaway Simone (Désirée Nosbusch, entrancingly opaque) loves the Neue Deutsche Welle pop singer known only as “R” (Bodo Staiger)… loves him so much, in fact, that she could just about eat him alive. And when she finally meets her idol—only to be callously treated by him as a disposable sex object—well, Simone gets the chance to really become one with her beloved forever. A hard, cool-to-the-touch, and utterly riveting slow-burn psychological thriller that, newly restored for its first ever US theatrical release, speaks to our age of parasocial obsession, featuring a sinister synth-pop soundtrack by Staiger’s own band, Rheingold, and a last act that’s finger-lickin’ good.

screenings.title: Collateral
screenings.description: Los Angeles cabbie Max Durocher (Jamie Foxx) is in for the toughest fare of his working life when he picks up one Vincent (Tom Cruise, natty in charcoal gray sharkskin suit), a jazz enthusiast and professional hitman who quite firmly insists that his driver accompany him on his evening’s rounds, leaving a trail of bodies in his wake. Shooting LA exteriors after dark with a then-state-of-the-art Sony F-900 digital camera, Mann gave his film a wholly distinctive texture—combining expressionistic smear with a new ability to pick up detail that would be lost on celluloid—and initiated a quiet revolution in low-light cinematography. A drum-tight character-based thriller, and the only film in which you can see Tom Cruise saying: “Yo, homie… Is that my briefcase?”

screenings.title: The Others
screenings.description: Having enjoyed a palpable international hit with his Abre Los Ojos—picked up for an American remake, under the title Vanilla Sky, by Tom Cruise—Amenábar made his English-language debut with The Others, a dolorous, deftly directed Old Dark House chiller set in the immediate aftermath of World War II, about a devoutly religious Englishwoman (Nicole Kidman, superb) living in a remote home in the Channel Island with her two young, severely photosensitive children and the strange goings-on that begin shortly after she takes on a trio of new servants. “Elegant… Creates more tension from atmosphere alone than most other horror films do from vats full of fake blood.” —The Times of London

screenings.title: The Apartment
screenings.description: Jack Lemmon is one anxious face in a sea of stooges at the New York insurance company where he toils, a passive nobody able to distinguish himself to his superiors only by letting boss Fred MacMurray use his shoebox apartment as a love nest, while his tentative romance with an elevator operator (Shirley MacLaine) plays out against a backdrop of boozy office Christmas parties, mocking holiday decorations, and mirthless cheer. Oh, and it’s a howl, too! The razor-sharp script by Wilder and I.A.L. Diamond gives the film its acerbic slice, while Joseph LaShelle’s elegant, cool black-and-white photography and the brittle tinkle of Adolf Deutsch’s jazz lounge score bring out the underlying sadness of this brilliantly bittersweet paradigm of the comedy-drama.

A sort-of sequel to Wong’s Days of Being Wild and In the Mood for Love, the ’60s-set 2046 revisits Tony Leung Chiu-wai’s Chow, now a suave science-fiction writer, to chronicle his various affairs with women (including Faye Wong, Zhang Ziyi, and Gong Li), acting as distractions now that his true love, Mrs. Chen (Maggie Cheung, seen in flashback), has disappeared. Intercutting scenes from Chow’s footloose life—several of these taking place on subsequent Christmas Eves—with scenes from his novel-in-progress, set in the titular year, it’s a film of voluptuous melancholy.

screenings.title: The City of Lost Children
screenings.description: Beginning with a Christmas Eve invasion by an army of nefarious Santas, Jeunet and Caro’s warped fairy tale follows a boy (Joseph Lucien) wandering the streets of a fog-shrouded harbor city populated by freaks and carnies, including the circus strongman One (Ron Perlman), and terrorized by Krank (Daniel Emilfork), the desiccant leader of a cult harvesting the dreams of kidnapped children. Eerie and imaginative, invested with unforgettable ambience by Darius Khondji’s green-gilled nocturnal photography.

screenings.title: Daughter of the Nile
screenings.description: A pivotal but little-screened film in Hou’s celebrated filmography, Daughter of the Nile acts as a sort of bridge between his breakthrough Coming of Age Trilogy and the trilogy of period-set films he made in collaboration with writer Wu Nien-jen. In this film, for the first time, Hou places contemporary Taipei center stage, telling the story of a young woman (pop star Lin Yang) trying to prevent her family from falling apart in a fast-changing city that offers its residents no sense of permanence or security. While Hou would explore Taipei’s complicated history in his films with Wu, in Daughter of the Nile he acutely diagnosed its present state.

screenings.title: Casino
screenings.description: Introduced by guest programmer Gina Telaroli on Friday, September 4 Dir. Martin Scorsese. 1995, 178 mins. 35mm. With Robert De Niro, Sharon Stone, Joe Pesci, James Woods, Don Rickles. Scorsese’s breathtaking epic about corruption in Sin City probes the minute details of casino operations and the larger scope of human betrayal. The film’s lavish spectacle—its flashing marquee lights, insider narration, dizzying quick cuts, and infinite rainbow of costumes—effectively reflect the characters’ emotions and confusion. In an Oscar-nominated performance of breathtaking force and vulnerability, Sharon Stone commands the screen as Ginger, a high-price call girl caught between the conditional affections of her husband, gangster Ace Rothstein (De Niro), and the machinations of psychotic Nicky Santoro (Pesci). As with GoodFellas, Casino was written by Nicholas Pileggi, based on his book. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Purchase tickets for Friday, September 4 at 6:30 p.m. Purchase tickets for Sunday, September 6, 1:00 p.m. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Shanghai Blues
screenings.description: Beginning against the backdrop of the Second Sino-Japanese War, the inimitable Tsui’s kinetic, ultra-stylish screwball comedy/historical romance/backstage musical—beautifully restored for the occasion of its 40th anniversary—is one of the most zestily entertaining and exuberantly colorful works of 1980s Hong Kong cinema. Kenny Bee’s nightclub clown and would-be songwriter meets-cute with chanteuse Sylvia Chang under a bridge during a 1937 bombing raid and the two make plans to find each other 10 years later, only to have their reunion in devastated postwar Shanghai elaborately and often hilariously complicated by intervening fate. An incredibly tender and terribly funny film, with Cantopop diva Sally Yeh giving a particularly inspired turn as Chang’s scatterbrained roommate.

screenings.title: American Job
screenings.description: Before obtaining cult immortality with American Movie, Smith made his auspicious feature debut with this microbudget, poker-faced mockumentary that approximates the style of an industrial film to follow Randy Scott (Randy Russell, credited as co-writer), a young man of limited skills and aspirations, as he listlessly makes his way through a litany of menial minimum-wage gigs: telemarketer, dishwasher, factory floor stooge, motel turn-down service, etc. What may in 1996 have seemed an unduly grim vision of the fate of the American working-class seems, 30 years on, nothing less than prophecy. “A miracle of Midwestern ingenuity and economy, Smith’s utterly remarkable first feature… [is[ as hilarious as it is is depressing.” —Amy Taubin, The Village Voice

screenings.title: Peking Opera Blues
screenings.description: Set in the newly established, vulnerable Republican China of 1913, Peking Opera Blues is a fizzily exuberant, chaotically colorful espionage thriller/screwball romance/slapstick social satire/costume drama pageant that bends genres and genders at will, wending together the stories of three irrepressible female protagonists—played by Sally Yeh, Brigitte Lin, and Cherie Chung, respectively here as a would-be star of the all-male Peking Opera stage, a warlord’s headstrong daughter, and a courtesan who’s copped a case of stolen jewels. Frenetic, filled with whiplash-inducing tonal shifts, frightfully enjoyable and, in the opinion of Quentin Tarantino, “one of the greatest films ever made.”

screenings.title: Delicatessen
screenings.description: The first feature by Jeunet and Caro, who had only completed a handful of shorts when they stunned the world with this antic, stylish debut—a skewed, funhouse mirror vision informed by comic strips, gonzo animation, and silent comedy. In a post-apocalyptic cityscape, an unemployed circus clown finds himself privy to the secrets of a butcher’s shop that has resorted to cannibalism. Shot in hues of burnished gold by Darius Khondji, this deliciously dark debut created an entire fallen world on a shoestring, becoming an art house phenomenon along the way.

screenings.title: American Doctor
screenings.language: English, Arabic, and Hebrew with English Subtitles
screenings.description: From Oscar®-nominated and Emmy® Award-winning filmmaker Poh Si Teng, American Doctor follows three American physicians— Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian—united by a single oath to save lives. After volunteering in besieged hospitals in Gaza, they return home determined to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind, taking their battle from the front lines of war to the halls of Congress.

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder, Hacks) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson, The X-Files, Sex Education), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

screenings.title: The Odyssey in 70mm
screenings.description: Christopher Nolan’s next film; The Odyssey stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, king of Ithaca, as he embarks on a perilous journey to return home after the Trojan War. Also starring Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson and Lupita Nyong’o, with Zendaya and Charlize Theron.

screenings.title: Free Lyric
screenings.description: Sat Sep 12: Who Moves America Q&A w/dir. Yael Bridge and prods. Yoni Golijov & Mars Verrone, moderated by Laura Poitras, at 6:55 s

screenings.title: The Odyssey in 70mm
screenings.description: Christopher Nolan’s next film; The Odyssey stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, king of Ithaca, as he embarks on a perilous journey to return home after the Trojan War. Also starring Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson and Lupita Nyong’o, with Zendaya and Charlize Theron.

screenings.title: Lightning Bug
screenings.description: When her son and granddaughter arrive to pressure Lydia (Lois Smith) into selling the family home, the fiercely independent 91-year-old former actress must prove she’s still capable of handling herself, especially once a strange young man crashes their dinner.

screenings.title: How to Divorce During the War
screenings.description: Vilnius, 2022. High-flying executive Marija chooses the worst possible moment to inform her husband Vytas she wants a divorce: just one day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Suddenly the couple must navigate separating in the middle of a refugee and mid-life crisis. As the reason for their divorce gradually becomes clear, the dissolution of the marriage and the turmoil of world events creates conflicts and opportunities for them both—and for their ever-observant young daughter.

screenings.title: Playtime
screenings.description: On official business in Paris, Tati’s beloved, bumbling alter-ego Monsieur Hulot discovers himself lost in a new, modern cityscape of midcentury modern glass cubes, gimcrack gadgets, squeaky pleather, and shiny chromium. A brilliant burlesque of the Bauhaus future c. 1967, using some of the most elaborate sets ever created for a French film, and an experimental narrative that has the rowdy democratic mob as its ensemble "hero."

screenings.title: Who Framed Roger Rabbit
screenings.description: Down-on-his-luck private eye Eddie Valiant is hired by cartoon producer R.K. Maroon to investigate an adultery scandal involving Jessica Rabbit, the sultry wife of Maroon’s biggest star, Roger Rabbit. But when Marvin Acme, Jessica’s alleged paramour and the owner of Toontown, is found murdered, the villainous Judge Doom vows to catch and destroy Roger.

screenings.title: Maddie's Secret
screenings.description: Tuesday, June 16 at 7:00: Sneak Preview + Q&A with John Early Wednesday, June 17 at 7:00: Sneak Preview + Q&A with John Early and Carla Lalli Friday, June 19 at 2:15: Q&A with John Early moderated by John Wilson Friday, June 19 at 4:45: Q&A with John Early moderated by Brace Belden Friday, June 19 at 7:15: Q&A with John Early moderated by Ivy Wolk Friday, June 10 at 9:45: Extended introduction by John Early Saturday, June 20 at 11:30: Q&A with John Early moderated by Julio Torres Saturday, June 20 at 2:15: Q&A with John Early moderated by Theda Hammel Saturday, June 20 at 4:45: Q&A with John Early moderated by Sarah Sherman Saturday, June 20 at 7:15: Q&A with John Early moderated by Amy Sedaris Saturday, June 20 at 9:45: Extended introduction by John Early

screenings.title: The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring
screenings.description: A meek Hobbit from the Shire and eight companions set out on a journey to destroy the powerful One Ring and save Middle Earth from the Dark Lord Sauron. Cast Alan Howard Noel Appleby Sean Astin Sala Baker Sean Bean Billy Boyd Orlando Bloom Ian McKellen Elijah Wood

screenings.title: Akira Re-release
screenings.description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988— World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo... As the leader of a group of young, robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy― the product of human experimentation— and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness…

screenings.title: The Salt Path
screenings.description: The profound story of husband and wife Raynor and Moth Winn (Jason Isaacs & Gillan Anderson), who embark on a 630-mile trek after being forcibly removed from their home. Hoping that in nature they will find solace and a sense of acceptance, they walk through the beautiful but rugged coastlines of South West England - a journey that is exhilarating, challenging, and liberating in equal measure. THE SALT PATH is a powerful portrayal of home, and how it can be lost and rediscovered in the most unexpected ways.

screenings.title: E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial
screenings.description: A world-conquering pop culture phenomenon on its original release, today it’s easier to see Spielberg’s boy-and-his-alien fable as the movie it always was—modest and familiar in its domestic setting, supremely sensitive to all the fun and the fear of childhood, and very often close to achieving the sublime. Abandoned on earth, a duck-walking alien longing to “Phone home” encounters a human boy who needs companionship, with unforgettable and heart-rending results.

screenings.title: The Last Picture Show
screenings.description: Peter Bogdanovich’s The Last Picture Show is the feature debut of Cybill Shepherd, includes the songs of Hank Williams and is one of the best movies in the 1970s. Based on Larry McMurtry’s semi-autobiographical novel and set in the early 1950s, Sonny Crawford is coming of age in the desolate town of Anarene, Texas. Sonny’s closest friends are his high school buddy Duane Jackson and his surrogate father Sam the Lion, whose tough-minded integrity stands in contrast to everyone around him. Eager to experiment with sex, Sony begins an affair with his coach’s wife. However, his understanding of the world is thrown into question when Sam the Lion suddenly dies, and his relationship with the coach’s wife proves emotionally complicated.

screenings.description: Marga en el DF / Mexico, U.S.A. (Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie) — In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima.

screenings.title: The Cycle of Love
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: In 1977, PK, a 23-year-old Delhi street artist from a poor, ‘untouchable’ family, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile cross-continent mission - to find Lotta, the woman who had captured his heart. A love story like no other, THE CYCLE OF LOVE is an inspiring, heart-warming, epic true-life adventure about the search for self-belief and risking everything for what your heart tells you.

screenings.title: Tony
screenings.description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles in the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

screenings.title: The Odyssey
screenings.description: Christopher Nolan’s newest film stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, king of Ithaca, as he embarks on a perilous journey to return home after the Trojan War. Also starring Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson and Lupita Nyong’o, with Zendaya and Charlize Theron.

screenings.title: Cocoon - One Summer of Girlhood
screenings.description: San and Mayu attend an all-girls school on a warm and tranquil island. When war reaches their shores, they are ordered to help nurse the wounded in a military hospital hidden away in a cave. Amidst escalating death and brutality, the friends struggle to find solace in their fragile lives. Based on the manga by Machiko Kyo, cocoon – One Summer of Girlhood is the debut feature from Yukimitsu Ina and animation studio SASAYURI, founded by former Studio Ghibli animator Hitomi Tateno. The project brings together legendary veteran animators like Akihiko Yamashita and Shinji Otsuka, known for their work on PRINCESS MONONOKE and THE BOY AND THE HERON, with a new, young generation of animating talent. Featuring a stirring score from kensuke ushio (A Silent Voice, Chainsaw Man), the film is a devastating yet beautiful plea for peace.

screenings.title: Union County (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor (Annette Deao), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future.

screenings.title: Steel Magnolias
screenings.description: A young beautician, newly arrived in a small Louisiana town, finds work at the local salon, where a small group of women share a close bond of friendship and welcome her into the fold.

screenings.title: Virginia Woolf’s Night & Day
screenings.description: Based on Virginia Woolf’s funniest novel, Night & Day follows passionate astronomer Katherine Hilbery as she does everything she can to avoid romantic love and marriage. Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: Hanging by a Wire
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: A routine school commute turns terrifying when a cable car’s wire snaps, leaving eight passengers — including six schoolboys — dangling 900 feet above a ravine in the remote Himalayan foothills. With no margin for error and a cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of rescuers must improvise under intense public scrutiny, racing against an invisible clock before disaster strikes live on television.

screenings.title: The Work in Progress
screenings.description: If you were invited to sit at a table with someone you’ve never met before and answer handwritten questions from a wooden box about the state of America, would you run the other way? The Work in Progress invites strangers from across generations and geographies to engage in candid discussions about America’s ever-evolving democracy, identity, and definitions of community — and where the heck we go from here. Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

screenings.title: Brailled It
screenings.description: Every year, the top under-18 Braille readers and writers from across the English-speaking world gather in Los Angeles to compete in the Braille Challenge. For one weekend, blind and low-vision kids are no longer the minority in the room. They make new friends, face off against old rivals, and chase a rare chance to be recognized not for their disability, but for their skill. In Brailled It, the camera is placed directly in their hands. As the kids document the competition themselves, their fragmented imagery and candid moments of nerves, boredom, joy, and triumph invite audiences to experience the event on their terms. Designed with audio description and accessibility at its core–not as an afterthought but as a fundamental creative tool–the film shifts authorship and perspective to the community on screen, revealing a world defined not by limitation, but by mastery, ambition, and the transformative power of literacy.

screenings.title: Love Me Tonight
screenings.description: Dir. Rouben Mamoulian. 1932, 88 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Maurice Chevalier, Jeanette MacDonald, Charles Ruggles. This complete and total comic delight of the early sound era, featuring music by Rodgers & Hart, is a constant dazzler from the always innovative Rouben Mamoulian (Applause, Dr. Jekyll and Mr, Hyde, Becky Sharp), whose cinematic experimentation knew no bounds or genre. Here, he dives into the Ruritanian musical, casting early-thirties superstar Maurice Chevalier as a jovial tailor who tries to collect on a bill from a Count—and falls in love with a princess. From its opening sequence, with the camera floating over the rooftops and through the streets of Paris (Paris, Hollywood, that is), Love Me Tonight was the first truly modern movie musical. The songs (including “Mimi” and “Isn’t It Romantic”) are perfectly integrated into the narrative, and Mamoulian showed how to turn a theatrical form into a cinematic experience. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: The Marching Band
screenings.description: A world-famous orchestra conductor discovers the brother he never knew he had -- a school cafeteria worker who plays trombone in a local marching band. Detecting his brother's exceptional musical talent, he takes it upon himself to rectify the injustice of fate. An equally hilarious and affecting crowd-pleaser that premiered at Cannes and became a French box office sensation starring Benjamin Lavernhe (My Donkey, My Lover & I) and Pierre Lottin (The Stranger).

screenings.title: Franz
screenings.description: Award-winning director Agnieszka Holland embarks on her most ambitious project to date, a biopic of the iconic 20th-century Czech writer Franz Kafka. Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Colony
screenings.description: Horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s (Train to Busan) new zombie thriller stars Gianna Jun as biology professor Se-jeong, who’s thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. Also starring Koo Kyo-hawn.

screenings.title: Gandahar
screenings.description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

screenings.title: Coyote vs Acme
screenings.description: Wile E. Coyote teams up with a struggling lawyer to sue the ACME Corporation in this romp.

screenings.title: A Brighter Summer Day
screenings.description: A sprawling and intimate evocation of the Taiwan of Yang’s teenage years: the outset of the 1960s, a period defined by street gang activity, the political repression of the Kuomintang military government, and the ubiquity of American pop culture. A Brighter Summer Day takes its inspiration from the story of the country’s first juvenile homicide, with Chang Chen’s brooding outsider just one figure in Yang’s bustling tapestry, regarded in seemingly serene long takes that bristle with repressed emotion.

screenings.title: The Sun Never Sets (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: Free-spirited Wendy (Dakota Fanning) is at a crossroads in her relationship with older divorced dad Jack (Jake Johnson, New Girl) that is only further complicated when an old flame (Cory Michael Smith, Sentimental Value) re-enters her life. Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
screenings.description: A queer director brings new blood to a slasher-film franchise in Jane Schoenbrun’s latest.

screenings.title: Tony
screenings.description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles into the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

screenings.title: The Invite

screenings.title: Finding Emily

Based on the manga by Machiko Kyo, cocoon – One Summer of Girlhood is the debut feature from Yukimitsu Ina and animation studio SASAYURI, founded by former Studio Ghibli animator Hitomi Tateno. The project brings together legendary veteran animators like Akihiko Yamashita and Shinji Otsuka, known for their work on PRINCESS MONONOKE and THE BOY AND THE HERON, with a new, young generation of animating talent. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.title: What Godmilow Taught
screenings.description: FILMMAKER IN PERSON!In 2012, Jill Godmilow wrote to Mireia Sallarès, moved by the film she had made in Mexico about women’s orgasms. For Godmilow, who offered to help distribute the film in the U.S., LAS MUERTES CHIQUITAS (THE LITTLE DEATHS) is not a documentary about a problem of Mexican women, it is a film about orgasms as a political issue that affects everyone and raises the question of who can take responsibility for it by speaking out. How to take responsibility for our problems, how to take charge of them by making political films, was the concern that had led Godmilow to engage years earlier with Harun Farocki’s documentary INEXTINGUISHABLE FIRE, which showed how napalm production during the Vietnam War effectively exempted its makers from any responsibility for it. The fact that Farocki’s film had not been seen in the U.S. and that the problem it raised had not gone away, Godmilow decided to recreate it, in order to involve herself in the problem and put it back into circulation. As a statement about what it means today to be an author, and taking account of this complexity by broadening and politicizing the chain of authorship, she titled her replica WHAT FAROCKI TAUGHT. The present film, WHAT GODMILOW TAUGHT (2014), is a film conversation in which Mireia Sallarès captures Jill Godmilow’s commitment to a political life. Sallarès’s film engages with an artistic practice in which having an idea entails a responsibility, and in which grappling with a political problem requires collaborating with others to make useful films.Followed by:Jill Godmilow ECSTATIC ORGASM 7.5-min excerpt from an unfinished film, digitalTotal running time: ca. 60 min.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: Two boyhood pals who have since drifted apart, played by Daniel London and musician Will Oldham, impulsively reunite for a camping and hiking trip in the verdant woods of the Pacific Northwest in Reichardt’s breakout sophomore feature, released 12 years after debut River of Grass. Dialogue is at a minimum in Reichardt’s serene, solemn film, but London and Oldham’s taciturn, intricately detailed performances—as well as the plangent score by Yo La Tengo and the evocative photographing of the landscape—speak volumes about middle-aged mournfulness and faded friendship. screenings.title: 9/11, Pgm 4: the Time We Killed (16mm)
screenings.description: So asks the Artist, one of three intertwined paranoiacs in Roger Copeland’s sprawling post-9/11, DIY, Brechtian fever dream. Proposing a twist on the axiom that the urge to destroy is also a creative urge, Copeland’s film suggests that all creativity is paranoid, and all paranoia is creative. It depicts a world that exists in “a state of semiotic arousal, a horniness for meaning.” Taking place in October of 2001, the film cuts between the story of a young girl who thinks the father that walked out on her family might be among the unrecovered dead at Ground Zero; the self-proclaimed BioEvangelist, who, in between compulsively consuming media coverage of the attacks’ aftermath in his basement chemistry lab, plans his own epistolary reckoning; and the aforementioned Artist, who monologues (livestreams?) from his studio about the ways the “death artists” have put art on the defensive.

screenings.title: Akira Re-release
screenings.description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988— World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo... As the leader of a group of young, robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy― the product of human experimentation— and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness…

screenings.title: Brailled It
screenings.description: Every year, the top under-18 Braille readers and writers from across the English-speaking world gather in Los Angeles to compete in the Braille Challenge. For one weekend, blind and low-vision kids are no longer the minority in the room. They make new friends, face off against old rivals, and chase a rare chance to be recognized not for their disability, but for their skill. In Brailled It, the camera is placed directly in their hands. As the kids document the competition themselves, their fragmented imagery and candid moments of nerves, boredom, joy, and triumph invite audiences to experience the event on their terms. Designed with audio description and accessibility at its core–not as an afterthought but as a fundamental creative tool–the film shifts authorship and perspective to the community on screen, revealing a world defined not by limitation, but by mastery, ambition, and the transformative power of literacy.

screenings.title: Roy Cohn/jack Smith
screenings.description: From one of the seminal theatrical events of the 1990s – Ron Vawter’s extraordinary performance piece ROY COHN/JACK SMITH – Godmilow crafts a dramatically deft, comic, and terrifying film diptych. Roy Cohn, the homophobic right-wing lawyer and sleazy back-room politico, thunders against the Sodom and Gomorrah of homosexuality at a banquet for the American Society for the Protection of the Family, while across town and light years away, the notorious underground filmmaker of FLAMING CREATURES fame, Jack Smith, in flamboyant harem drag, constructs his own private resistance theater from fragments of Arabian Nights kitsch, avant-garde film feuds, and passionate B-movie camp. Vawter performs both men exquisitely in this film about the closet, where silence is powerful, but from which both of these infamous homosexuals from the repressive and punishing 1950s convey privileged knowledge of Queerness in brilliant performances of their own – Cohn using politics as a form of drag and Smith turning drag into an extraordinary form of politics, pathos, and jouissance. Cohn and Smith had nothing in common except their homosexuality and their death from AIDS in the late 1980s; Vawter, who accepts and produces both men through his own voice and body, would himself die of AIDS, just six months after the film was shot.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: After Hours
screenings.description: Cheech and Chong! Sultry sculptress Linda Fiorentino! Bad Brains! These are but a few of the characters that Midtown computer jockey Paul Hackett (Griffin Dunne) will encounter when venturing into the wilds of a pre-gentrification downtown New York without a penny to his name or the means to get back home in Scorsese’s bravura black comedy of class resentment, all-pervasive paranoia, and creeping castration anxiety, in which the director can be briefly spotted manning a spotlight at punk rock dive Club Berlin. As Dick Miller’s diner waiter explains to the hapless Hackett, “Different rules apply when it gets this late…” As true of the city in 1985 as it is today.

Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei Kuroda (Masaki Suda), a brilliant yet dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon. Helped by his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and his most loyal generals, Murashige must uncover the truth before the castle falls.

screenings.title: Daughter of the Nile
screenings.description: A pivotal but little-screened film in Hou’s celebrated filmography, Daughter of the Nile acts as a sort of bridge between his breakthrough Coming of Age Trilogy and the trilogy of period-set films he made in collaboration with writer Wu Nien-jen. In this film, for the first time, Hou places contemporary Taipei center stage, telling the story of a young woman (pop star Lin Yang) trying to prevent her family from falling apart in a fast-changing city that offers its residents no sense of permanence or security. While Hou would explore Taipei’s complicated history in his films with Wu, in Daughter of the Nile he acutely diagnosed its present state.

screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.description: Vilnius, 2022. High-flying executive Marija chooses the worst possible moment to inform her husband Vytas she wants a divorce: just one day before Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Suddenly the couple must navigate separating in the middle of a refugee and mid-life crisis. As the reason for their divorce gradually becomes clear, the dissolution of the marriage and the turmoil of world events creates conflicts and opportunities for them both—and for their ever-observant young daughter.

screenings.title: Who Framed Roger Rabbit
screenings.description: Down-on-his-luck private eye Eddie Valiant is hired by cartoon producer R.K. Maroon to investigate an adultery scandal involving Jessica Rabbit, the sultry wife of Maroon’s biggest star, Roger Rabbit. But when Marvin Acme, Jessica’s alleged paramour and the owner of Toontown, is found murdered, the villainous Judge Doom vows to catch and destroy Roger.

Cast Bruce Allpress John Bach Sala Baker Orlando Bloom Billy Boyd Ian McKellen Viggo Mortensen Elijah Wood

screenings.title: Akira Re-release
screenings.description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988— World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo... As the leader of a group of young, robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy― the product of human experimentation— and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness…

screenings.title: The Salt Path
screenings.description: The profound story of husband and wife Raynor and Moth Winn (Jason Isaacs & Gillan Anderson), who embark on a 630-mile trek after being forcibly removed from their home. Hoping that in nature they will find solace and a sense of acceptance, they walk through the beautiful but rugged coastlines of South West England - a journey that is exhilarating, challenging, and liberating in equal measure. THE SALT PATH is a powerful portrayal of home, and how it can be lost and rediscovered in the most unexpected ways.

screenings.title: The Last Picture Show
screenings.description: Peter Bogdanovich’s The Last Picture Show is the feature debut of Cybill Shepherd, includes the songs of Hank Williams and is one of the best movies in the 1970s. Based on Larry McMurtry’s semi-autobiographical novel and set in the early 1950s, Sonny Crawford is coming of age in the desolate town of Anarene, Texas. Sonny’s closest friends are his high school buddy Duane Jackson and his surrogate father Sam the Lion, whose tough-minded integrity stands in contrast to everyone around him. Eager to experiment with sex, Sony begins an affair with his coach’s wife. However, his understanding of the world is thrown into question when Sam the Lion suddenly dies, and his relationship with the coach’s wife proves emotionally complicated.

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma in 35mm
screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder, Hacks) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson, The X-Files, Sex Education), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

screenings.title: Tony
screenings.description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles in the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

screenings.title: Cocoon - One Summer of Girlhood
screenings.description: San and Mayu attend an all-girls school on a warm and tranquil island. When war reaches their shores, they are ordered to help nurse the wounded in a military hospital hidden away in a cave. Amidst escalating death and brutality, the friends struggle to find solace in their fragile lives. Based on the manga by Machiko Kyo, cocoon – One Summer of Girlhood is the debut feature from Yukimitsu Ina and animation studio SASAYURI, founded by former Studio Ghibli animator Hitomi Tateno. The project brings together legendary veteran animators like Akihiko Yamashita and Shinji Otsuka, known for their work on PRINCESS MONONOKE and THE BOY AND THE HERON, with a new, young generation of animating talent. Featuring a stirring score from kensuke ushio (A Silent Voice, Chainsaw Man), the film is a devastating yet beautiful plea for peace.

(Director and Screenwriter: Gabriela Ortega, Producers: Karla Luna Cantú, Natalia Gonzalez, Eugenio Valero, Carlos López Estrada, Valerie Bush, Stacy Perskie) — In the wake of Selena Quintanilla’s murder, Marga’s life takes an unexpected turn at 21 weeks pregnant during a surprise visit to Mexico City. Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima.

screenings.title: The Cycle of Love
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: In 1977, PK, a 23-year-old Delhi street artist from a poor, ‘untouchable’ family, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile cross-continent mission - to find Lotta, the woman who had captured his heart. A love story like no other, THE CYCLE OF LOVE is an inspiring, heart-warming, epic true-life adventure about the search for self-belief and risking everything for what your heart tells you.

screenings.title: Union County (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor (Annette Deao), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future.

screenings.title: The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas
screenings.description: Miss Mona (Dolly Parton) runs the Chicken Ranch, a brothel with a long history in a small Texas town. The locals have a good relationship with the institution, and Mona is respected in the community. The sheriff, Ed Earl Dodd (Burt Reynolds), also looks out for the Chicken Ranch due to his past with Miss Mona. However, when pious reporter Melvin Thorpe (Dom DeLuise) exposes the brothel, outside interests want it shut down, putting the governor (Charles Durning) in a tough spot.

screenings.title: Shanghai Blues
screenings.description: Beginning against the backdrop of the Second Sino-Japanese War, the inimitable Tsui’s kinetic, ultra-stylish screwball comedy/historical romance/backstage musical—beautifully restored for the occasion of its 40th anniversary—is one of the most zestily entertaining and exuberantly colorful works of 1980s Hong Kong cinema. Kenny Bee’s nightclub clown and would-be songwriter meets-cute with chanteuse Sylvia Chang under a bridge during a 1937 bombing raid and the two make plans to find each other 10 years later, only to have their reunion in devastated postwar Shanghai elaborately and often hilariously complicated by intervening fate. An incredibly tender and terribly funny film, with Cantopop diva Sally Yeh giving a particularly inspired turn as Chang’s scatterbrained roommate.

screenings.title: Jason and the Argonauts
screenings.description: The story is that of heroic Jason sailing far and wide questing for the Golden Fleece of lore, but it’s never looked like this before, thanks to stop-motion superstar Ray Harryhausen’s ability to put flesh on mythic fancy. An energetic epic in Eastmancolor, with Bernard Herrmann contributing soundtrack fanfare and Harryhausen realizing a veritable menagerie of monsters, including the animate statue of Talos, the hissing Hydra and, in the film’s piece de resistance, seven scimitar-wielding skeletons who face Todd Armstrong’s Jason in a swashbuckling battle royale.

screenings.title: Hanging by a Wire
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: A routine school commute turns terrifying when a cable car’s wire snaps, leaving eight passengers — including six schoolboys — dangling 900 feet above a ravine in the remote Himalayan foothills. With no margin for error and a cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of rescuers must improvise under intense public scrutiny, racing against an invisible clock before disaster strikes live on television.

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: Gardens of Stone
screenings.description: U.S., 1987 Directed by Francis Ford Coppola Starring James Caan, Anjelica Huston, James Earl Jones, D.B. Sweeney Based on Nicholas Proffitt’s novel 111 min. 35mm. “Tells the stories of several relationships at this outpost far behind the front lines. The film introduces the kid (D. B. Sweeney), his immediate superior (James Caan) and the sergeant above him (James Earl Jones). And then there is the girl the kid would like to marry (Mary Stuart Masterson), and there is Caan’s new girlfriend (Anjelica Huston), who works for the Washington Post and considers the Vietnam War to be genocide.” – Roger Ebert Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: Boorman and the Devil
screenings.description: Boorman and the Devil is a 2025 American documentary film about John Boorman’s 1977 horror film Exorcist II: The Heretic, which almost ended his career. Boorman, Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher are among the cast and crew interviewed in David Kittredge’s deep dive into a notorious flop.

screenings.title: Franz
screenings.description: Award-winning director Agnieszka Holland embarks on her most ambitious project to date, a biopic of the iconic 20th-century Czech writer Franz Kafka. Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.title: The Work in Progress
screenings.description: If you were invited to sit at a table with someone you’ve never met before and answer handwritten questions from a wooden box about the state of America, would you run the other way? The Work in Progress invites strangers from across generations and geographies to engage in candid discussions about America’s ever-evolving democracy, identity, and definitions of community — and where the heck we go from here. Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

screenings.title: Virginia Woolf’s Night & Day
screenings.description: Based on Virginia Woolf’s funniest novel, Night & Day follows passionate astronomer Katherine Hilbery as she does everything she can to avoid romantic love and marriage. Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

screenings.title: Late Fame
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “A loving and lovely sensibility runs through LATE FAME, a fond and wise understanding of why some people want to become artists without making much art and why other people quit making it altogether.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “[A] lovely and bittersweet drama... Dafoe has rarely been so tender, playing a man allowing himself to dream again for the first time in forever.” – Tim Grierson, A/V Club “Like a wonderful little poem... Samy Burch, who also wrote the astute Oscar®-nominated script for 2023’s MAY DECEMBER, has crafted another subtle but powerful work.” – Kyle Smith, The Wall Street Journal “Lyrical and enchanting... Dafoe’s performance is like a slowly unfolding wildflower.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Willem Dafoe is low key and magnificent as a former poet seemingly rescued from obscurity... In a prolific career filled with complex and striking characters, the role of Ed Saxberger is a subdued but particularly rich one for Dafoe, himself a veteran of the downtown arts scene.” – Sheri Linden, The Hollywood Reporter “LATE FAME is a deliciously acidic examination of the thin line between creative aspiration and pretentious poseurdom.” – Wendy Ide, Screen International

screenings.title: Casino
screenings.description: Introduced by guest programmer Gina Telaroli on Friday, September 4 Dir. Martin Scorsese. 1995, 178 mins. 35mm. With Robert De Niro, Sharon Stone, Joe Pesci, James Woods, Don Rickles. Scorsese’s breathtaking epic about corruption in Sin City probes the minute details of casino operations and the larger scope of human betrayal. The film’s lavish spectacle—its flashing marquee lights, insider narration, dizzying quick cuts, and infinite rainbow of costumes—effectively reflect the characters’ emotions and confusion. In an Oscar-nominated performance of breathtaking force and vulnerability, Sharon Stone commands the screen as Ginger, a high-price call girl caught between the conditional affections of her husband, gangster Ace Rothstein (De Niro), and the machinations of psychotic Nicky Santoro (Pesci). As with GoodFellas, Casino was written by Nicholas Pileggi, based on his book. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. screenings.description: A world-famous orchestra conductor discovers the brother he never knew he had -- a school cafeteria worker who plays trombone in a local marching band. Detecting his brother's exceptional musical talent, he takes it upon himself to rectify the injustice of fate. An equally hilarious and affecting crowd-pleaser that premiered at Cannes and became a French box office sensation starring Benjamin Lavernhe (My Donkey, My Lover & I) and Pierre Lottin (The Stranger).

screenings.title: Colony
screenings.description: Horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s (Train to Busan) new zombie thriller stars Gianna Jun as biology professor Se-jeong, who’s thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. Also starring Koo Kyo-hawn.

screenings.title: Gandahar
screenings.description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

screenings.title: The Umbrellas of Cherbourg
screenings.description: Dir. Jacques Demy. 1964, 92 mins. France. DCP. With Catherine Deneuve, Nino Castelnuovo, Marc Michel, Anne Vernon. One of the most exquisite romances ever filmed, Jacques Demy’s gorgeous, melancholy tale of young love thwarted by harsh reality is completely sung through to an unforgettable score by the great Michel Legrand. Deneuve commands the screen as the daughter of an umbrella-shop owner who falls hard for a sweet-faced young car mechanic, who is eventually sent off to fight in the Algerian War. Perhaps the tenderest film of the French New Wave, Demy’s lovely operetta is a triumph of cinematography, costume design, art direction, and music. When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

A chance teleprinter error at work and a wrongful arrest, however, set Sam on a course for real adventure, one involving his dream girl’s truck-driving double, a suspected terrorist (Robert De Niro), a freakshow cocktail party, plastic surgery disasters, and much more outlandishness besides. “A melancholy, joke-ridden view of the horribleness of where we are now and the worst horribleness of where we’re heading… It’s like a stoned, slapstick 1984: a nightmare comedy in which the comedy is just an aspect of the nightmarishness.” —Pauline Kael, The New Yorker

Figures familiar from myth—including Pegasus, the two-headed dog Dioskilos, and a memorably loathsome Medusa—share screentime with inventions original to the film, notably Andromeda’s ogrish betrothed, Calibos, and the gold-wrought mechanical owl, Bubo, in this irresistible flight of fancy, a film of “blood and thunder and lots of gory details… presented with enormous gusto and style.” [Roger Ebert, Chicago Sun-Times]

screenings.title: Boorman and the Devil
screenings.description: Boorman and the Devil is a 2025 American documentary film about John Boorman’s 1977 horror film Exorcist II: The Heretic, which almost ended his career. Boorman, Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher are among the cast and crew interviewed in David Kittredge’s deep dive into a notorious flop.

screenings.title: Hearts of Darkness: a Filmmaker’s Apocalypse
screenings.description: U.S., 1991 Directed by Fax Bahr, George Hickenlooper, Eleanor Coppola Featuring Eleanor Coppola, Francis Ford Coppola, Robert Duvall, Dennis Hopper, George Lucas, John Milius, Martin Sheen Approx. 96 min. 4K restoration. In the late 1970s, director Francis Ford Coppola, accompanied by his family and cast and crew, travelled to the Philippines to begin work on what would become APOCALYPSE NOW. But it soon became one of the most notorious shoots in cinema history, spiraling into a hellish, life-threatening nightmare. Chronicling the drama was Coppola’s wife, the late Eleanor Coppola, who shot extensive behind-the-scenes footage of the shoot in 16mm, and recorded audio interviews with her husband and others involved in the movie’s making. In the early ’90s, Eleanor turned her 16mm footage and audio interviews over to filmmakers George Hickenlooper and Fax Bahr, who then interwove it with new interviews with the movie’s cast members (including Martin Sheen and Dennis Hopper) and observers (like George Lucas). After a year of editing, the new documentary debuted at the Cannes Film Festival. It had its New York theatrical premiere at Film Forum. Says James Mockoski, Film Archivist and Restoration Supervisor at American Zoetrope, “For the past 30 years, Eleanor’s 16mm behind-the-scenes footage has been three to four generations removed from the original elements. For this new release and restoration of the documentary, Francis decided to scan the original sources in 4K. The extensive excerpts from the feature are now presented in their original 2.39:1 aspect ratio, rather than being letterboxed into a 4x3 frame.” Restored at American Zoetrope and graded at Roundabout Entertainment. Restoration supervised by Francis Ford Coppola. Special thanks to James Mockoski, American Zoetrope's Film Archivist and Restoration Supervisor.

screenings.title: Hanging by a Wire
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: A routine school commute turns terrifying when a cable car’s wire snaps, leaving eight passengers — including six schoolboys — dangling 900 feet above a ravine in the remote Himalayan foothills. With no margin for error and a cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of rescuers must improvise under intense public scrutiny, racing against an invisible clock before disaster strikes live on television.

screenings.title: The Lake House | 2006 Movies
screenings.description: A lonely doctor who once occupied an unusual lakeside house begins to exchange love letters with its former resident, a frustrated architect. They must try to unravel the mystery behind their extraordinary romance before it’s too late.

screenings.title: The Work in Progress
screenings.description: If you were invited to sit at a table with someone you’ve never met before and answer handwritten questions from a wooden box about the state of America, would you run the other way? The Work in Progress invites strangers from across generations and geographies to engage in candid discussions about America’s ever-evolving democracy, identity, and definitions of community — and where the heck we go from here. Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: Blood Brunch
screenings.description: Calling all Bloodeaters, Love Butchers and Neon Maniacs! The lights go down, the screen lights up and every one of your senses is flooded with ghastly terror from beyond the fetid grave. Spend your Sundays drenched in blood and quivering in fear with a mystery movie—as in, we don’t tell you what we’re showing until you see the title on the screen—that is at least 20 years old.

screenings.title: Brailled It
screenings.description: Every year, the top under-18 Braille readers and writers from across the English-speaking world gather in Los Angeles to compete in the Braille Challenge. For one weekend, blind and low-vision kids are no longer the minority in the room. They make new friends, face off against old rivals, and chase a rare chance to be recognized not for their disability, but for their skill. In Brailled It, the camera is placed directly in their hands. As the kids document the competition themselves, their fragmented imagery and candid moments of nerves, boredom, joy, and triumph invite audiences to experience the event on their terms. Designed with audio description and accessibility at its core–not as an afterthought but as a fundamental creative tool–the film shifts authorship and perspective to the community on screen, revealing a world defined not by limitation, but by mastery, ambition, and the transformative power of literacy.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

screenings.title: Late Fame
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “A loving and lovely sensibility runs through LATE FAME, a fond and wise understanding of why some people want to become artists without making much art and why other people quit making it altogether.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “[A] lovely and bittersweet drama... Dafoe has rarely been so tender, playing a man allowing himself to dream again for the first time in forever.” – Tim Grierson, A/V Club “Like a wonderful little poem... Samy Burch, who also wrote the astute Oscar®-nominated script for 2023’s MAY DECEMBER, has crafted another subtle but powerful work.” – Kyle Smith, The Wall Street Journal “Lyrical and enchanting... Dafoe’s performance is like a slowly unfolding wildflower.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Willem Dafoe is low key and magnificent as a former poet seemingly rescued from obscurity... In a prolific career filled with complex and striking characters, the role of Ed Saxberger is a subdued but particularly rich one for Dafoe, himself a veteran of the downtown arts scene.” – Sheri Linden, The Hollywood Reporter “LATE FAME is a deliciously acidic examination of the thin line between creative aspiration and pretentious poseurdom.” – Wendy Ide, Screen International

screenings.title: Frances Ha
screenings.description: Dir. Noah Baumbach. 2013, 86 mins. U.S. DCP. With Greta Gerwig, Mickey Sumner, Adam Driver, Michael Zegen, Charlotte D’Ambroise, Grace Gummer. With its lustrous black-and-white cinematography, clever and moving script by Greta Gerwig and Noah Baumbach, and vibrant central performance by Gerwig as the eponymous Frances, this lovely pocket portrait of an “undatable” young woman navigating early twenty-first century New York friendships, relationships, post-college malaise, and exorbitant ATM fees has already proven to be a generational cornerstone. Endlessly rewatchable, Frances Ha moves with the fleet-footed lightness and knowing of a French New Wave classic yet with a tenderness and empathy that feels tuned into the specific experiences of living in a city that’s both unforgiving and undeniable. screenings.title: The Little Deaths / Las Muertes Chiquitas
screenings.description: “In 2006 the Barcelona artist and filmmaker Mireia Sallarès began interviewing, in complete intimacy, about thirty Mexican women, about just that: being women in Mexico and their sexual experiences – their experience with pleasure and also with violence. The result is LAS MUERTES CHIQUITAS, ‘the little deaths’, which, like the French ‘la petite mort’, is a slangy euphemism in Spanish for female orgasm, the post-orgasmic state of unconsciousness that some experience after sex. This wild, five-hour film is revolutionary. […] Sallarès uses the simplest of means, filming by herself, entirely in medium close-ups, as she interviews, among many others, two anthropologists, a performance artist, an AIDS worker, a few sex-workers, a cabaret artist, two psychoanalysts, an historian, two ex-nuns, a journalist, a cross-dressing bisexual-tranny, a housekeeper, an actress, a philosopher, two guerillas, even exiled women from other countries…. She asks them to talk about, at first, their own orgasms. What emerge are extraordinary stories and images of pleasure, and often damage.“The film’s subtitle, ‘An unfinished story of pleasure and violence’, helps connect the dots. There is abundant sexual violence against and around women in Mexico, and effective resistance. Sallarès’s correspondents are prepared to talk about their histories and so the film goes there – not just to the violence but also to the relationship between violence and sexuality, and soon enough to violence, sex, pleasure and spiritual release. These are models to learn from and admire. The critic Helena Braunštajn says this film is a place ‘where pleasure is related to armed struggle, feminicide, transsexuality, women’s liberation theology, prostitution, illness, exile, the plurality of Mexican identity, and the ethical commitment of art to socio-political reality.’ One woman says orgasm is ‘like grabbing onto the wings of an angel who lowers me down to the ground.’ Enough said.” –Jill GodmilowCLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness…

screenings.title: Apocalypse Now: Final Cut
screenings.description: U.S., 1979/2019 Directed by Francis Ford Coppola Inspired by Joseph Conrad’s novel, Heart of Darkness Starring Marlon Brando, Martin Sheen, Robert Duvall, Dennis Hopper, Frederic Forrest, Laurence Fishburne WINNER Cannes Film Festival – Palme d’Or, 1979 WINNER Academy Awards® – Best Cinematography, Best Sound, 1980 Approx. 182 min. “Starts with what proves to be a nightmare: a stand of pale green palm trees, ominous air-beating chops, the fleeting blurs of attack helicopters, a sudden rush of flame engulfing the trees as, in magically perfect rhythm, Jim Morrison’s high, thin voice croons, ‘This is the end...’ Then the dreamer of this recurring vision appears mingled with his own demonic images, in a Saigon hotel room during the Vietnam war, drunk, stunned, virtually deranged—an American captain named Benjamin Willard (Martin Sheen). screenings.title: The Treasure of Bitch Islands
screenings.description: A phantasmagoric, definition-defying film from perhaps France’s premier underground filmmaker, The Treasure of Bitch Islands begins with the mysterious disappearance of an engineer who has discovered a new energy source, and follows a post-nuclear Ulysses’s voyage to locate the substances used in the engineer’s formula, only to be found and harvested on an island of mad scientists and headhunters. An anarchic allegory with a punky sensibility, part Guy Maddin pastiche, part surrealist mix-and-match, and pure cult classic. “The shoot was madness, and some of us risked our lives a few times, especially while doing a scene on the edge of this huge volcano. Ossang was really more like a rock star than a film director… I shot the film completely inspired by him and his energy, even if I was sometimes terrified.” —Darius Khondji

screenings.title: Himala
screenings.description: Despite being considered the second-most important Filipino director after Brocka in his home country, the work of Second Golden Age director Ishmael Bernal has not been screened as often abroad in recent years, in part due to print scarcity. Notorious for his sharp wit, the openly gay Bernal was a subversive ironist and a committed feminist. His films frequently used the roles of women to skewer what he saw as a sick society under the Marcos regime, best summed up by a line from his provocatively-titled essay Why The Martial Law Will Affect Your Sex Life: “Here we are, being practically ruled by a stranger who shall parade the chills and fevers of his ego and what are we going to do about it? We are going to be gripped by hysteria, that’s what.” This attitude culminated in the consensus pick for his masterpiece, Himala (1982), a study of the blind faith of the Philippines and the grip of hysteria that comes with it – it has only been vindicated with the country’s election of another Ferdinand Marcos to the Presidency. Bernal has subsequently remained a touchstone for the two key figures from the subsequent Third Golden Age: Spectacle favorites Lav Diaz and Raya Martin.
