screenings.title: Barbara Hammer: Love Is Where You Find It
screenings.description: The erotic unfurls as a vital force connecting self, lover, and collective. Barbara Hammer left behind a monumental body of work unified in its fiercely political perspective and bold exploration of lesbian life. Her earliest short films materialized from the ashes of postwar American life, as long-established virtues of womanhood were being rejected and a new vision was beginning to form. As Hammer put it in her own memoir: “The 70s were a glorious time of feminist ideals and lesbian bed-hopping.” These works spotlight Hammer’s sustained investment in collective queer worldmaking, mobilizing eroticism as a social force inseparable from emergent forms of lesbian visibility and activist formation. Total runtime: Approx. 77 min. Double Strength U.S., 1978 Approx. 14 min. A poetic meditation on the arc of a lesbian relationship from the charge of erotic beginnings, the rupture of conflict, to the settled ground of enduring friendship. Hammer draws directly onto celluloid and layers mirrored images of bodies moving asynchronously, while musings on love, life, and death drift through the soundtrack. Woven through are a trapeze duet performed by Hammer and aerial dancer Terry Sendgraff, and portraits of the couple. Dyketactics U.S.,1974 Approx. 4 min. Inspired by Maya Deren’s Meshes of the Afternoon, Hammer set off on a motorcycle with a Super-8 camera to make what became widely regarded as the first lesbian lovemaking film by a lesbian filmmaker. Calling it her “popular lesbian commercial,” she compressed 110 images of sensual touching into rapid montage, cut across A, B, C, and D rolls in what she termed “kinaesthetic” editing. Superdyke U.S., 1975 Approx. 17 min. A militant feminist lesbian comedy from the early liberation era, following a troupe of shield-bearing Amazons as they storm San Francisco—City Hall, bus lines, Macy’s, an erotic art museum—before retreating to the utopic countryside. The film gave voice to the city’s emerging lesbian community, channeling Hammer’s ongoing fascination with communal life, her handheld camera capturing both bystanders’ shock and her participants’ joy. Sync Touch U.S.,1981 Approx. 10 min. In one of her most explicit attempts to construct a haptic cinema, Hammer explores a lesbian-feminist aesthetic that positions touch and sight as the twin foundations of a “new cinema,” binding sexuality and filmmaking together with a scientific inquiry into the sense of touch. Painting and collaging directly onto the 16mm film strip, and using an optical printer to loop, layer, and manipulate the shots, she distorts the imagery to manifest this physicality. Audience U.S., 1982 Approx. 32 min. A 16mm diary and historical archive, this major work of sapphic ethnography finds Hammer interviewing moviegoers at screenings of her films in San Francisco, London, Toronto, and Montreal. She captures an array of reactions and reflections on both her films and depictions of lesbians on screen; the work doubling as a self-portrait, refracted through the eyes of her audience. Programmed by Andrea Torres Presented with support from The R.G. Rifkind Foundation Endowment for Queer Cinema and The Roy Lichtenstein Foundation Fund Images courtesy of the Estate of Barbara Hammer, New York and Electronic Arts Intermix (EAI), New York.

Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. screenings.description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988— World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo... As the leader of a group of young, robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy― the product of human experimentation— and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. screenings.description: San and Mayu attend an all-girls school on a warm and tranquil island. When war reaches their shores, they are ordered to help nurse the wounded in a military hospital hidden away in a cave. Amidst escalating death and brutality, the friends struggle to find solace in their fragile lives. Based on the manga by Machiko Kyo, cocoon – One Summer of Girlhood is the debut feature from Yukimitsu Ina and animation studio SASAYURI, founded by former Studio Ghibli animator Hitomi Tateno. The project brings together legendary veteran animators like Akihiko Yamashita and Shinji Otsuka, known for their work on PRINCESS MONONOKE and THE BOY AND THE HERON, with a new, young generation of animating talent. Featuring a stirring score from kensuke ushio (A Silent Voice, Chainsaw Man), the film is a devastating yet beautiful plea for peace.

A sort-of sequel to Wong’s Days of Being Wild and In the Mood for Love, the ’60s-set 2046 revisits Tony Leung Chiu-wai’s Chow, now a suave science-fiction writer, to chronicle his various affairs with women (including Faye Wong, Zhang Ziyi, and Gong Li), acting as distractions now that his true love, Mrs. Chen (Maggie Cheung, seen in flashback), has disappeared. Intercutting scenes from Chow’s footloose life—several of these taking place on subsequent Christmas Eves—with scenes from his novel-in-progress, set in the titular year, it’s a film of voluptuous melancholy.

screenings.title: Brailled It
screenings.description: Every year, the top under-18 Braille readers and writers from across the English-speaking world gather in Los Angeles to compete in the Braille Challenge. For one weekend, blind and low-vision kids are no longer the minority in the room. They make new friends, face off against old rivals, and chase a rare chance to be recognized not for their disability, but for their skill. In Brailled It, the camera is placed directly in their hands. As the kids document the competition themselves, their fragmented imagery and candid moments of nerves, boredom, joy, and triumph invite audiences to experience the event on their terms. Designed with audio description and accessibility at its core–not as an afterthought but as a fundamental creative tool–the film shifts authorship and perspective to the community on screen, revealing a world defined not by limitation, but by mastery, ambition, and the transformative power of literacy.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... screenings.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
screenings.description: U.S., 1992 Directed by Francis Ford Coppola Based on Bram Stoker’s novel Starring Gary Oldman, Winona Ryder, Anthony Hopkins, Keanu Reeves Approx. 128 min. 35mm. “The film begins, as it should, with the tragic story of Vlad the Impaler, who went off to fight the Crusades and returned to find that his beloved wife, hearing he was dead, had killed herself. Coppola’s plot, from a screenplay by James V. Hart, exists precisely between London, where this modern age is just dawning, and Transylvania, which still sleeps unhealthily in the past. We meet a young attorney (Keanu Reeves) who has been asked to journey out to Dracula’s castle to arrange certain real estate transactions. Reeves’ carriage, driven by a man whose hands are claws, hurtles at the edges of precipices until he is finally discharged in the darkness to be met and taken to Dracula’s castle. There, everything is more or less as we expect it, only much more so. Count Dracula (Gary Oldman) waits here as he has for centuries for the return of his dead bride, and when he sees a photograph of Reeves’ fiancee, Mina Murray (Winona Ryder), he knows his wait has been rewarded at last. She lives again.” – Roger Ebert Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: Mysterious Skin
screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.title: Akira Re-release
screenings.description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988— World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo... As the leader of a group of young, robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy― the product of human experimentation— and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness…

screenings.title: Der Fan
screenings.description: Teen runaway Simone (Désirée Nosbusch, entrancingly opaque) loves the Neue Deutsche Welle pop singer known only as “R” (Bodo Staiger)… loves him so much, in fact, that she could just about eat him alive. And when she finally meets her idol—only to be callously treated by him as a disposable sex object—well, Simone gets the chance to really become one with her beloved forever. A hard, cool-to-the-touch, and utterly riveting slow-burn psychological thriller that, newly restored for its first ever US theatrical release, speaks to our age of parasocial obsession, featuring a sinister synth-pop soundtrack by Staiger’s own band, Rheingold, and a last act that’s finger-lickin’ good.

screenings.title: Women on the Verge of a Nervous Breakdown
screenings.description: Capping an incredible eight-year creative partnership with Almodóvar, repeat collaborator Carmen Maura here plays voice actress Pepa, who, abandoned by her lover, has resolved to kill herself by downing a batch of gazpacho laced with sleeping pills. That’s just the start of the orgy of unhinged behavior that makes up Almodóvar’s gaudy, cheeky screwball melodrama about Shiite terrorist cells and romance on the rocks, a camp romp celebration of emotional excess that has all the makings of an obscure cult classic, yet improbably became the highest-grossing Spanish film of all time upon release, and did its part in putting co-star Antonio Banderas on the international stage.

screenings.title: Millennium Mambo
screenings.description: A stylish and seductive submersion into the techno-scored neon nightlife of Taipei, Hou’s much-misunderstood marvel stars Shu Qi (The Assassin) as an aimless bar hostess drifting away from her blowhard boyfriend and towards Jack Kao’s suave, sensitive gangster. Structured as a flashback to the then-present from the then-future of 2011, it’s a transfixing trance-out of a movie, drenched in club lights, ecstatic endorphin-rush exhilaration, and a nagging undercurrent of ennui. Hou and longtime cinematographer Lee here break from their familiar pattern of elegantly composed long shot long takes to create something both more intimate and hectic, a film whose shallow-focus images, jittery camerawork, and cramped locations evoke both the claustrophobic character of Taiwan’s capital city and, in Lee’s words, “the feeling of youth.”

screenings.description: U.S./Germany/Italy, 2007 Written and directed by Francis Ford Coppola Starring Tim Roth, Alexandra Maria Lara, Bruno Ganz Based on Mircea Eliade’s novella 124 min. 35mm. Professor of language and philosophy Dominic Matei (Tim Roth) is struck by lightning and ages backwards from 70 to 40 in a week, attracting the world and the Nazis. While on the run, the professor meets a young woman (Alexandra Maria Lara) who has her own experience with a lightning storm. Not only does Dominic find love again, but her new abilities hold the key to his research. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: Wet Hot American Summer: 25th Anniversary Labor Day Screening
screenings.description: 25th Anniversary Labor Day Screening Dir. David Wain. 2001, 97 mins. U.S. DCP. With Paul Rudd, Janeane Garofalo, Elizabeth Banks, David Hyde Pierce, Ken Marino, Christopher Meloni, Molly Shannon. Set in Maine in summer 1981, Wet Hot American Summer follows the slapstick exploits of a group of sexually desperate (and often confused) camp counselors too busy trying to hook up to care much about the kids they’re supposed to be watching. One of the funniest movies of the twenty-first century, David Wain’s low-budget 2001 sendup of eighties summer camp comedies, co-written by Michael Showalter, is an endlessly quotable, primo gag-fest that shows both satirical mercilessness and sweet tenderness towards its subject and milieu, and features an incredible cast of comic talents. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth (ages 3–17) / discounted for MoMI members ($7–$11). There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: The Marching Band
screenings.description: A world-famous orchestra conductor discovers the brother he never knew he had -- a school cafeteria worker who plays trombone in a local marching band. Detecting his brother's exceptional musical talent, he takes it upon himself to rectify the injustice of fate. An equally hilarious and affecting crowd-pleaser that premiered at Cannes and became a French box office sensation starring Benjamin Lavernhe (My Donkey, My Lover & I) and Pierre Lottin (The Stranger).

screenings.title: Colony
screenings.description: Horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s (Train to Busan) new zombie thriller stars Gianna Jun as biology professor Se-jeong, who’s thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. Also starring Koo Kyo-hawn.

screenings.title: Gandahar
screenings.description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

screenings.title: Finding Emily
screenings.description: When a lovesick musician is given the wrong number for his dream girl, he teams up with a driven psychology student to find her. Together, they spark a hilarious campus-wide frenzy that tests their own hearts and ambitions along the way.

screenings.title: Cocoon - One Summer of Girlhood
screenings.description: San and Mayu attend an all-girls school on a warm and tranquil island. When war reaches their shores, they are ordered to help nurse the wounded in a military hospital hidden away in a cave. Amidst escalating death and brutality, the friends struggle to find solace in their fragile lives. Based on the manga by Machiko Kyo, cocoon – One Summer of Girlhood is the debut feature from Yukimitsu Ina and animation studio SASAYURI, founded by former Studio Ghibli animator Hitomi Tateno. The project brings together legendary veteran animators like Akihiko Yamashita and Shinji Otsuka, known for their work on PRINCESS MONONOKE and THE BOY AND THE HERON, with a new, young generation of animating talent. Featuring a stirring score from kensuke ushio (A Silent Voice, Chainsaw Man), the film is a devastating yet beautiful plea for peace.

screenings.title: Mysterious Skin
screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma in 35mm
screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder, Hacks) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson, The X-Files, Sex Education), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

screenings.title: Akira Re-release
screenings.description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988— World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo... As the leader of a group of young, robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy― the product of human experimentation— and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness…

screenings.title: Tony
screenings.description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles in the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “What is your damage, Heather?” Cynical, surreal and viciously funny, this dark high school comedy remains one of the most influential teen movies ever. Iconic performances from 80s luminaries Winona Ryder, Shannen Doherty and Christian Slater, and a cornucopia of gleefully nasty putdowns (“Lick it up baby. Lick. It. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: The Cycle of Love
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: In 1977, PK, a 23-year-old Delhi street artist from a poor, ‘untouchable’ family, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile cross-continent mission - to find Lotta, the woman who had captured his heart. A love story like no other, THE CYCLE OF LOVE is an inspiring, heart-warming, epic true-life adventure about the search for self-belief and risking everything for what your heart tells you.

screenings.title: Brazil
screenings.description: Ground into despairing dust by his routine as a low-level bureaucrat in an Orwellian near-future—drabulously conceived as a junk shop jumble by art directors Norman Garwood and Maggie Gray—Sam (Jonathan Pryce) takes flight only in his imagination, where he plays the winged savior to distressed damsel Kim Griest. A chance teleprinter error at work and a wrongful arrest, however, set Sam on a course for real adventure, one involving his dream girl’s truck-driving double, a suspected terrorist (Robert De Niro), a freakshow cocktail party, plastic surgery disasters, and much more outlandishness besides. “A melancholy, joke-ridden view of the horribleness of where we are now and the worst horribleness of where we’re heading… It’s like a stoned, slapstick 1984: a nightmare comedy in which the comedy is just an aspect of the nightmarishness.” —Pauline Kael, The New Yorker

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: The Apartment
screenings.description: Jack Lemmon is one anxious face in a sea of stooges at the New York insurance company where he toils, a passive nobody able to distinguish himself to his superiors only by letting boss Fred MacMurray use his shoebox apartment as a love nest, while his tentative romance with an elevator operator (Shirley MacLaine) plays out against a backdrop of boozy office Christmas parties, mocking holiday decorations, and mirthless cheer. Oh, and it’s a howl, too! The razor-sharp script by Wilder and I.A.L. Diamond gives the film its acerbic slice, while Joseph LaShelle’s elegant, cool black-and-white photography and the brittle tinkle of Adolf Deutsch’s jazz lounge score bring out the underlying sadness of this brilliantly bittersweet paradigm of the comedy-drama.

screenings.title: Boorman and the Devil
screenings.description: Boorman and the Devil is a 2025 American documentary film about John Boorman’s 1977 horror film Exorcist II: The Heretic, which almost ended his career. Boorman, Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher are among the cast and crew interviewed in David Kittredge’s deep dive into a notorious flop.

screenings.description: A routine school commute turns terrifying when a cable car’s wire snaps, leaving eight passengers — including six schoolboys — dangling 900 feet above a ravine in the remote Himalayan foothills. With no margin for error and a cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of rescuers must improvise under intense public scrutiny, racing against an invisible clock before disaster strikes live on television.

screenings.title: Brailled It
screenings.description: Every year, the top under-18 Braille readers and writers from across the English-speaking world gather in Los Angeles to compete in the Braille Challenge. For one weekend, blind and low-vision kids are no longer the minority in the room. They make new friends, face off against old rivals, and chase a rare chance to be recognized not for their disability, but for their skill. In Brailled It, the camera is placed directly in their hands. As the kids document the competition themselves, their fragmented imagery and candid moments of nerves, boredom, joy, and triumph invite audiences to experience the event on their terms. Designed with audio description and accessibility at its core–not as an afterthought but as a fundamental creative tool–the film shifts authorship and perspective to the community on screen, revealing a world defined not by limitation, but by mastery, ambition, and the transformative power of literacy.

screenings.description: U.S., 1986 Directed by Francis Ford Coppola Starring Kathleen Turner, Nicolas Cage, Barry Miller, Catherine Hicks, Jim Carrey, Helen Hunt Approx. 103 min. 35mm. “Peggy Sue Bodell (Kathleen Turner) isn’t even sure she wants to go to her 25th high school reunion. Recently separated from Charlie (Nicolas Cage), the husband she had to marry at 18, even the idea of turning up where everyone will ask, ‘Where’s Crazy Charlie?,’ the wackiest businessman in TV ads, makes her cringe... As they’re crowning the Reunion King and Queen, Peggy Sue faints, coming to in 1960, a 43-year-old in an 18-year-old’s body. She knows the future all too well, from panty hose to the Pill. She’s seen Charlie give up his dreams of being a singer and slip into the family business—with a bit of philandering on the side. Apparently stuck reliving her last weeks of high school, should she should muck with her destiny or not?” – Sheila Benson, Los Angeles Times

screenings.title: The Salt Path
screenings.description: The profound story of husband and wife Raynor and Moth Winn (Jason Isaacs & Gillan Anderson), who embark on a 630-mile trek after being forcibly removed from their home. Hoping that in nature they will find solace and a sense of acceptance, they walk through the beautiful but rugged coastlines of South West England - a journey that is exhilarating, challenging, and liberating in equal measure. THE SALT PATH is a powerful portrayal of home, and how it can be lost and rediscovered in the most unexpected ways.

screenings.title: The Cycle of Love
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: In 1977, PK, a 23-year-old Delhi street artist from a poor, ‘untouchable’ family, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile cross-continent mission - to find Lotta, the woman who had captured his heart. A love story like no other, THE CYCLE OF LOVE is an inspiring, heart-warming, epic true-life adventure about the search for self-belief and risking everything for what your heart tells you.

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “What is your damage, Heather?” Cynical, surreal and viciously funny, this dark high school comedy remains one of the most influential teen movies ever. Iconic performances from 80s luminaries Winona Ryder, Shannen Doherty and Christian Slater, and a cornucopia of gleefully nasty putdowns (“Lick it up baby. Lick. It. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma in 35mm
screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder, Hacks) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson, The X-Files, Sex Education), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

screenings.title: Akira Re-release
screenings.description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988— World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo... As the leader of a group of young, robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy― the product of human experimentation— and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness…

But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

screenings.title: Franz
screenings.description: Award-winning director Agnieszka Holland embarks on her most ambitious project to date, a biopic of the iconic 20th-century Czech writer Franz Kafka. Conceived as a kaleidoscopic mosaic, the film follows the imprint Kafka left on the world from his birth in 19th-century Prague to his death in post-WW1 Vienna. Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: A Sad and Beautiful World
screenings.description: In this sweeping love story that spans three decades of passion, heartbreak and hope, Nino and Yasmina find themselves drawn together by a magnetic relationship. As they face an impossible choice between love and survival, they must decide if they want to build a family and chart a path to happiness in Lebanon, despite the tragedies ravaging the country. In Arabic with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Onslaught
screenings.description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

screenings.title: Virginia Woolf’s Night & Day
screenings.description: Based on Virginia Woolf’s funniest novel, Night & Day follows passionate astronomer Katherine Hilbery as she does everything she can to avoid romantic love and marriage. Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: American Doctor
screenings.language: English, Arabic, and Hebrew with English Subtitles
screenings.description: From Oscar®-nominated and Emmy® Award-winning filmmaker Poh Si Teng, American Doctor follows three American physicians— Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian—united by a single oath to save lives. After volunteering in besieged hospitals in Gaza, they return home determined to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind, taking their battle from the front lines of war to the halls of Congress.

screenings.title: The Work in Progress
screenings.description: If you were invited to sit at a table with someone you’ve never met before and answer handwritten questions from a wooden box about the state of America, would you run the other way? The Work in Progress invites strangers from across generations and geographies to engage in candid discussions about America’s ever-evolving democracy, identity, and definitions of community — and where the heck we go from here. Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

screenings.title: Hanging by a Wire
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: A routine school commute turns terrifying when a cable car’s wire snaps, leaving eight passengers — including six schoolboys — dangling 900 feet above a ravine in the remote Himalayan foothills. With no margin for error and a cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of rescuers must improvise under intense public scrutiny, racing against an invisible clock before disaster strikes live on television.

screenings.title: A Brighter Summer Day
screenings.description: A sprawling and intimate evocation of the Taiwan of Yang’s teenage years: the outset of the 1960s, a period defined by street gang activity, the political repression of the Kuomintang military government, and the ubiquity of American pop culture. A Brighter Summer Day takes its inspiration from the story of the country’s first juvenile homicide, with Chang Chen’s brooding outsider just one figure in Yang’s bustling tapestry, regarded in seemingly serene long takes that bristle with repressed emotion.

screenings.title: Delicatessen
screenings.description: The first feature by Jeunet and Caro, who had only completed a handful of shorts when they stunned the world with this antic, stylish debut—a skewed, funhouse mirror vision informed by comic strips, gonzo animation, and silent comedy. In a post-apocalyptic cityscape, an unemployed circus clown finds himself privy to the secrets of a butcher’s shop that has resorted to cannibalism. Shot in hues of burnished gold by Darius Khondji, this deliciously dark debut created an entire fallen world on a shoestring, becoming an art house phenomenon along the way.

screenings.title: The Rainmaker
screenings.description: U.S., 1997 Directed by Francis Ford Coppola Based on the John Grisham novel Starring Matt Damon, Claire Danes, Jon Voight, Danny DeVito, Mary Kay Place, Teresa Wright, Dean Stockwell Approx. 135 min. “We’re back in ingénue Southern lawyer territory, following law school grad Rudy Baylor (Damon) through his inaugural case to a mercurial triumph against the odds. So far, so insipid; thankfully, the story is less the usual addled potboiler than a diary of civil litigation—centring on Rudy’s pursuit of a giant insurance company accused of stalling on health claims arising from policies marketed to the poor and unrepresented, such as his client Donny Ray Black (Whitworth). Rudy describes the dilemma of his calling in voice-over, musing over ideals and corruptions, compromises and lawyer jokes. His pilgrim’s progress leads us through an entertaining gallery of lawyerly archetypes. There’s the cynic, Rudy’s long sold-out adversary Leo F. Drummond (Voight); the corrupt, his low-life employer Bruiser Stone (Rourke); and the merely ignoble, his ‘paralawyer’ assistant Deck Schifflet (DeVito). There’s a wider perspective on the legal action, too, counterpointing Rudy’s ‘rainmaking’ lawsuit with both a damp squib of another case, and a subplot involving Danes’ abused wife which suggests the limitations of the law.” – Time Out Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

screenings.title: Late Fame
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “A loving and lovely sensibility runs through LATE FAME, a fond and wise understanding of why some people want to become artists without making much art and why other people quit making it altogether.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “[A] lovely and bittersweet drama... Dafoe has rarely been so tender, playing a man allowing himself to dream again for the first time in forever.” – Tim Grierson, A/V Club “Like a wonderful little poem... Samy Burch, who also wrote the astute Oscar®-nominated script for 2023’s MAY DECEMBER, has crafted another subtle but powerful work.” – Kyle Smith, The Wall Street Journal “Lyrical and enchanting... Dafoe’s performance is like a slowly unfolding wildflower.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Willem Dafoe is low key and magnificent as a former poet seemingly rescued from obscurity... In a prolific career filled with complex and striking characters, the role of Ed Saxberger is a subdued but particularly rich one for Dafoe, himself a veteran of the downtown arts scene.” – Sheri Linden, The Hollywood Reporter “LATE FAME is a deliciously acidic examination of the thin line between creative aspiration and pretentious poseurdom.” – Wendy Ide, Screen International

Detecting his brother's exceptional musical talent, he takes it upon himself to rectify the injustice of fate. An equally hilarious and affecting crowd-pleaser that premiered at Cannes and became a French box office sensation starring Benjamin Lavernhe (My Donkey, My Lover & I) and Pierre Lottin (The Stranger).

screenings.description: Wile E. Coyote teams up with a struggling lawyer to sue the ACME Corporation in this romp.

screenings.title: Union County
screenings.description: Will Poulter and Noah Centineo deliver pitch-perfect performances as brothers Cody and Jack Parsons, each navigating a court-mandated drug rehabilitation program in a pocket of rural Ohio hit hard by the opioid epidemic. Provided with hope for the first time since their struggles began and with the support of a tireless counselor (Annette Deao), the brothers work toward a brighter, sober future.

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
screenings.description: A queer director brings new blood to a slasher-film franchise in Jane Schoenbrun’s latest.

screenings.title: The Sun Never Sets
screenings.description: Free-spirited Wendy (Dakota Fanning) is at a crossroads in her relationship with older divorced dad Jack (Jake Johnson, New Girl) that is only further complicated when an old flame (Cory Michael Smith, Sentimental Value) re-enters her life. Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

screenings.title: The Invite
screenings.description: A dinner party spirals into unexpected places in this star-studded portrait of marriage.

screenings.title: Gandahar
screenings.description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

screenings.description: Regarded as one of the best musicals in film, SINGIN' IN THE RAIN proves to be a timeless classic to this day. The film explores the struggles of a Hollywood production studio in the late 1920s as they are forced to transition to "talkies." With classic songs like “Make em’ Laugh” and “Good Morning” this wonderful musical comedy is a staple in cinematic history.

screenings.title: Star Trek Iv: the Voyage Home + S1e28
screenings.description: Living in exile on the planet Vulcan, the ragtag former crew of the USS Enterprise steal a starship after receiving a planetary distress call from Earth: a space probe has entered into orbit around Earth, disabled global power on the planet and evaporated the oceans. Captain Kirk (William Shatner), Spock (Leonard Nimoy) and the rest of the officers travel back in time to retrieve now-extinct humpback whales, which Spock has deduced will communicate with the probe and send it away from Earth. Bonus Content: Includes Season 1 Episode 28 "The City on the Edge of Forever" (50 minutes) never before seen on the big screen.

screenings.description: Beginning with a Christmas Eve invasion by an army of nefarious Santas, Jeunet and Caro’s warped fairy tale follows a boy (Joseph Lucien) wandering the streets of a fog-shrouded harbor city populated by freaks and carnies, including the circus strongman One (Ron Perlman), and terrorized by Krank (Daniel Emilfork), the desiccant leader of a cult harvesting the dreams of kidnapped children. Eerie and imaginative, invested with unforgettable ambience by Darius Khondji’s green-gilled nocturnal photography.

screenings.title: Brailled It
screenings.description: Every year, the top under-18 Braille readers and writers from across the English-speaking world gather in Los Angeles to compete in the Braille Challenge. For one weekend, blind and low-vision kids are no longer the minority in the room. They make new friends, face off against old rivals, and chase a rare chance to be recognized not for their disability, but for their skill. In Brailled It, the camera is placed directly in their hands. As the kids document the competition themselves, their fragmented imagery and candid moments of nerves, boredom, joy, and triumph invite audiences to experience the event on their terms. Designed with audio description and accessibility at its core–not as an afterthought but as a fundamental creative tool–the film shifts authorship and perspective to the community on screen, revealing a world defined not by limitation, but by mastery, ambition, and the transformative power of literacy.

screenings.title: The Odyssey
screenings.description: Odysseus fights monsters and menaces as he returns with his soldiers from the Trojan War.

screenings.title: Workingman's Death
screenings.description: A protege of fellow Austrian Ulrich Seidl, Glawogger was occasionally painted with the brush of “provocateur,” but his deep empathy, humor, and relentless curiosity guides his films even through the most challenging subject matter. His “Globalization Trilogy” is a triptych of documentaries loosely dealing with the effects of shifting economic markets and modernization on some of the world’s most disenfranchised workers — though Glawogger disliked the “Globalization” framing, eschewing academic detachment to emphasize his audience and subjects’ shared humanity. In each of these films, Glawogger avoids ethnographic trappings by placing his protagonists center stage, never trivializing or overtly romanticizing them even as they experience some of the harshest conditions imaginable.

Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

Hinton, and signalled by Coppola as ‘Camus for kids’, RUMBLE FISH does indeed have a hero figure (Rourke) who belongs to a former age of existential ‘outsiders’, coasting through the world in an insulated state of deafness and colour blindness from too many rumbles. His kid brother (Dillon) idolises him, but is too careless to see the damage done to all concerned by the continuous gang-fights of frightful violence but no importance.” – Time Out Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court, plunging the fortress into fear and suspicion. With Oda’s army closing in and a traitor hiding among his ranks, Murashige is forced into an uneasy alliance with Kanbei Kuroda (Masaki Suda), a brilliant yet dangerous strategist held prisoner in the dungeon. Helped by his wife Chiyoho (Yuriko Yoshitaka) and his most loyal generals, Murashige must uncover the truth before the castle falls.

screenings.title: Mysterious Skin
screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.title: I Want Your Sex
screenings.description: In the latest from New Queer Cinema pioneer Araki (“Mysterious Skin”), I Want Your Sex tells the story of Elliot (Cooper Hoffman), a kind-hearted if unmotivated twenty-something whose fantasies quickly come true when he lands a job with renowned artist and provocateur Erika Tracy (Olivia Wilde). When Erika breaks down office boundaries and takes Elliot on as her sexual muse and subordinate, their sexually charged relationship makes him question his own desires, boundaries and relationships with his uptight girlfriend (Charli xcx) and repressed roommate (Chase Sui Wonders). As the stakes heighten and power dynamics shift, the film mixes satire, romantic comedy, mystery and murder through the colorful and edgy visual language for which Araki is known.

A love story like no other, THE CYCLE OF LOVE is an inspiring, heart-warming, epic true-life adventure about the search for self-belief and risking everything for what your heart tells you.

screenings.title: The Sun Never Sets
screenings.description: Free-spirited Wendy (Dakota Fanning) is at a crossroads in her relationship with older divorced dad Jack (Jake Johnson, New Girl) that is only further complicated when an old flame (Cory Michael Smith, Sentimental Value) re-enters her life. Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

screenings.title: Tony

screenings.title: From Dusk Till Dawn
screenings.description: Directed by Robert Rodriguez and written by Quentin Tarantino, From Dusk Till Dawn is everything you’d want in an all action horror vampire movie. Escaped convict brothers with mental issues? Check. Sexy vampire queens? Check. Dirty jokes and deadly monsters? Check, check. Harvey Keitel as a bow-wielding pastor who lost his faith? Check. What starts out as questionable morality of two criminals who kidnap a family in order to flee into Mexico turns into a struggle of mortality as they surprisingly find themselves in an overnight battle to save their souls from bloodthirsty biker vampires. From Dusk Till Dawn is a fantastically unique twist on the generic vampire tale: unwitting visitors who find themselves fighting the undead done as only the Rodriguez/Tarantino combo could do. A big screen must see.

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “What is your damage, Heather?” Cynical, surreal and viciously funny, this dark high school comedy remains one of the most influential teen movies ever. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

THE SALT PATH is a powerful portrayal of home, and how it can be lost and rediscovered in the most unexpected ways.

screenings.title: Peking Opera Blues
screenings.description: Set in the newly established, vulnerable Republican China of 1913, Peking Opera Blues is a fizzily exuberant, chaotically colorful espionage thriller/screwball romance/slapstick social satire/costume drama pageant that bends genres and genders at will, wending together the stories of three irrepressible female protagonists—played by Sally Yeh, Brigitte Lin, and Cherie Chung, respectively here as a would-be star of the all-male Peking Opera stage, a warlord’s headstrong daughter, and a courtesan who’s copped a case of stolen jewels. Frenetic, filled with whiplash-inducing tonal shifts, frightfully enjoyable and, in the opinion of Quentin Tarantino, “one of the greatest films ever made.”

Winner of the FIPRESCI Prize at the Cannes Film Festival, Ducournau’s gruesome drama of sexual awakening and campus cannibalism found its way onto a great many best-of-the-year lists, and announced the appearance of a new virtuoso of body horror.

screenings.title: 9/11, Pgm 3: Circling Zero
screenings.description: So asks the Artist, one of three intertwined paranoiacs in Roger Copeland’s sprawling post-9/11, DIY, Brechtian fever dream. Proposing a twist on the axiom that the urge to destroy is also a creative urge, Copeland’s film suggests that all creativity is paranoid, and all paranoia is creative. It depicts a world that exists in “a state of semiotic arousal, a horniness for meaning.” Taking place in October of 2001, the film cuts between the story of a young girl who thinks the father that walked out on her family might be among the unrecovered dead at Ground Zero; the self-proclaimed BioEvangelist, who, in between compulsively consuming media coverage of the attacks’ aftermath in his basement chemistry lab, plans his own epistolary reckoning; and the aforementioned Artist, who monologues (livestreams?) from his studio about the ways the “death artists” have put art on the defensive.

screenings.description: A routine school commute turns terrifying when a cable car’s wire snaps, leaving eight passengers — including six schoolboys — dangling 900 feet above a ravine in the remote Himalayan foothills. With no margin for error and a cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of rescuers must improvise under intense public scrutiny, racing against an invisible clock before disaster strikes live on television.

screenings.title: Akira Re-release
screenings.description: Iconic and game-changing, AKIRA is the definitive anime masterpiece! Katsuhiro Otomo's landmark cyberpunk classic obliterated the boundaries of Japanese animation and forced the world to look into the future. AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988— World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo... As the leader of a group of young, robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy― the product of human experimentation— and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness…

screenings.title: The Marching Band
screenings.description: A world-famous orchestra conductor discovers the brother he never knew he had -- a school cafeteria worker who plays trombone in a local marching band. Detecting his brother's exceptional musical talent, he takes it upon himself to rectify the injustice of fate. An equally hilarious and affecting crowd-pleaser that premiered at Cannes and became a French box office sensation starring Benjamin Lavernhe (My Donkey, My Lover & I) and Pierre Lottin (The Stranger).

screenings.title: Colony
screenings.description: Horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s (Train to Busan) new zombie thriller stars Gianna Jun as biology professor Se-jeong, who’s thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. Also starring Koo Kyo-hawn.

screenings.title: The Work in Progress

screenings.title: The Odyssey
screenings.description: Christopher Nolan’s newest film stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, king of Ithaca, as he embarks on a perilous journey to return home after the Trojan War. Also starring Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson and Lupita Nyong’o, with Zendaya and Charlize Theron.

screenings.title: Gandahar
screenings.description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

screenings.language: English, Arabic, and Hebrew with English Subtitles

screenings.title: The Sun Never Sets (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: Free-spirited Wendy (Dakota Fanning) is at a crossroads in her relationship with older divorced dad Jack (Jake Johnson, New Girl) that is only further complicated when an old flame (Cory Michael Smith, Sentimental Value) re-enters her life. Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

screenings.title: Finding Emily
screenings.description: When a lovesick musician is given the wrong number for his dream girl, he teams up with a driven psychology student to find her. Together, they spark a hilarious campus-wide frenzy that tests their own hearts and ambitions along the way.

screenings.title: Mysterious Skin
screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma in 35mm
screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder, Hacks) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson, The X-Files, Sex Education), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “What is your damage, Heather?” Cynical, surreal and viciously funny, this dark high school comedy remains one of the most influential teen movies ever. Iconic performances from 80s luminaries Winona Ryder, Shannen Doherty and Christian Slater, and a cornucopia of gleefully nasty putdowns (“Lick it up baby. Lick. It. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: The Cycle of Love
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: In 1977, PK, a 23-year-old Delhi street artist from a poor, ‘untouchable’ family, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile cross-continent mission - to find Lotta, the woman who had captured his heart. A love story like no other, THE CYCLE OF LOVE is an inspiring, heart-warming, epic true-life adventure about the search for self-belief and risking everything for what your heart tells you.

screenings.title: Akira Re-release

AKIRA's arrival shattered traditional thinking, creating space for future generations of ground-breaking movies. July, 1988— World War III breaks loose. Then, in 2019, in megalopolis Tokyo... As the leader of a group of young, robust delinquents, Kaneda spent his nights tearing through the urban wastes, racing his motorbike against rival groups. One night while riding with his gang, his friend Tetsuo suddenly encounters a strange boy― the product of human experimentation— and is injured in the ensuing crash. Shortly thereafter, a military squadron appears on the scene to take the boy and Tetsuo away to an army research facility. Determined to free Tetsuo from capture, Kaneda sneaks into the army research lab. However, a regimen of extreme experimental procedures has awakened a new power in his friend, and now he is consumed by madness…

When war reaches their shores, they are ordered to help nurse the wounded in a military hospital hidden away in a cave. In Brailled It, the camera is placed directly in their hands. Designed with audio description and accessibility at its core–not as an afterthought but as a fundamental creative tool–the film shifts authorship and perspective to the community on screen, revealing a world defined not by limitation, but by mastery, ambition, and the transformative power of literacy.

Franz gives audiences a brand new perspective on the life of the man behind the literary giant. In Czech and German with English subtitles.

Amidst escalating death and brutality, the friends struggle to find solace in their fragile lives. Based on the manga by Machiko Kyo, cocoon – One Summer of Girlhood is the debut feature from Yukimitsu Ina and animation studio SASAYURI, founded by former Studio Ghibli animator Hitomi Tateno. The project brings together legendary veteran animators like Akihiko Yamashita and Shinji Otsuka, known for their work on PRINCESS MONONOKE and THE BOY AND THE HERON, with a new, young generation of animating talent. Featuring a stirring score from kensuke ushio (A Silent Voice, Chainsaw Man), the film is a devastating yet beautiful plea for peace.

screenings.title: Late Fame

An equally hilarious and affecting crowd-pleaser that premiered at Cannes and became a French box office sensation starring Benjamin Lavernhe (My Donkey, My Lover & I) and Pierre Lottin (The Stranger).

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma
screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

screenings.title: Brailled It
screenings.description: Every year, the top under-18 Braille readers and writers from across the English-speaking world gather in Los Angeles to compete in the Braille Challenge. For one weekend, blind and low-vision kids are no longer the minority in the room. They make new friends, face off against old rivals, and chase a rare chance to be recognized not for their disability, but for their skill. In Brailled It, the camera is placed directly in their hands. As the kids document the competition themselves, their fragmented imagery and candid moments of nerves, boredom, joy, and triumph invite audiences to experience the event on their terms. Designed with audio description and accessibility at its core–not as an afterthought but as a fundamental creative tool–the film shifts authorship and perspective to the community on screen, revealing a world defined not by limitation, but by mastery, ambition, and the transformative power of literacy.

screenings.title: Coyote vs Acme

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma

screenings.title: The Sun Never Sets
screenings.description: Free-spirited Wendy (Dakota Fanning) is at a crossroads in her relationship with older divorced dad Jack (Jake Johnson, New Girl) that is only further complicated when an old flame (Cory Michael Smith, Sentimental Value) re-enters her life. Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

screenings.title: The Invite
screenings.description: A dinner party spirals into unexpected places in this star-studded portrait of marriage.

screenings.title: Gandahar
screenings.description: An entire civilization must confront its destiny in alternative-animation pioneer René Laloux’s final feature, a cult classic of mind-bending science fiction. In a distant world, a merciless army of automata attacks Gandahar, turning its peace-loving people to stone. Hoping to discover the source of these Men of Metal, a council of matriarchs enlists the brave yet inexperienced warrior Sylvain (Pierre-Marie Escourro), who, while journeying through his planet’s outer regions, teams up with the Deformed, a race cast out from Gandahar after failed science experiments rendered them mutants. Soon, Sylvain learns that a gargantuan brain called Metamorphis (Georges Wilson) is responsible for his utopian society’s strife and—together with the beautiful Airelle (Catherine Chevallier)—travels through time to defeat him, in the process risking their lives and Gandahar’s very existence. Featuring stunningly surreal creatures and wondrously bizarre environments designed by renowned comic-book artist Caza, Gandahar is a visceral, visionary head-trip in which animation opens a gateway to the furthest reaches of the imagination.

screenings.title: Tony

screenings.title: The Cycle of Love
screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: In 1977, PK, a 23-year-old Delhi street artist from a poor, ‘untouchable’ family, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile cross-continent mission - to find Lotta, the woman who had captured his heart. A love story like no other, THE CYCLE OF LOVE is an inspiring, heart-warming, epic true-life adventure about the search for self-belief and risking everything for what your heart tells you.

Cast: Camila Santana, David Palacio, Xabiani Ponce de León, Andrea de Fátima.

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “What is your damage, Heather?” Cynical, surreal and viciously funny, this dark high school comedy remains one of the most influential teen movies ever. Iconic performances from 80s luminaries Winona Ryder, Shannen Doherty and Christian Slater, and a cornucopia of gleefully nasty putdowns (“Lick it up baby. Lick. It. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: The Godfather Part Ii
screenings.description: U.S., 1974 Directed by Francis Ford Coppola Starring Al Pacino, Robert De Niro, Diane Keaton, John Cazale, Robert Duvall WINNER Academy Awards® – Best Picture, Best Director, Best Supporting Actor (Rober De Niro), Best Adapted Screenplay, Best Art Direction, Best Original Score, 1975 Approx. 202 min. 4K restoration. Both prequel and sequel to the original, as Pacino’s Michael consolidates his empire after dabbling in Cuban futures and vets the family for weaklings, while Oscar®-winner Robert De Niro, as the young Godfather-to-be, takes on the bosses of turn-of-the-20th-century Little Italy. Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: True North
screenings.description: “This propulsive cinematic confrontation with Canada’s anti-Black racism explores the pivotal, yet often overlooked, Canadian civil rights movement. Filmmaker Michèle Stephenson (AMERICAN PROMISE; STATELESS; GOING TO MARS: THE NIKKI GIOVANNI PROJECT) artfully weaves a haunting soundscape with dynamic archival footage and intimate new interviews, immersing us in Black life in 1960s Montreal. The film culminates in the 1969 Sir George Williams Affair, where 200 students, many of them Haitian immigrants fleeing the Duvalier regime, occupied a ninth-floor computer lab at Sir George Williams University (now Concordia) to protest blatant institutional bigotry. This rare footage feels hauntingly prescient against the backdrop of recent student protests, serving as a stark reminder that these cycles of resistance are deeply etched in our collective history. By shining a light on these unsung stories, Stephenson reframes the 1960s civil rights movement not as a strictly American phenomenon, but as a continent-wide, ongoing struggle for survival, justice, and dignity.” –FULL FRAME DOCUMENTARY FILM FESTIVALPreceded by:Dawn Wilkinson DANDELIONS 1995, 5 min, 16mm“In DANDELIONS, Dawn Wilkinson – a Black Canadian woman – bears witness to the experience of being made to feel like an outsider in one’s own home, in one’s own landscape. At one point, Wilkinson observes, ‘I’m Canadian…It’s popular enough to sell beer, but no one can define what it means. And yet they do, they define it every time they ask me where I’m from.’ DANDELIONS is a beautiful and eloquent film that deploys the techniques of a lyrical, interiorized cinema to lay bare the ways in which Western societies foster an idea of whiteness as ‘neutral’ and everything else as ‘other,’ and to illustrate the psychic toll on those who exist outside this construct.” –Jed Rapfogel, CINEASTETotal running time: ca. 105 min.Michèle Stephenson will be here in person!CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Metropolis (1927)

As the reason for their divorce gradually becomes clear, the dissolution of the marriage and the turmoil of world events creates conflicts and opportunities for them both—and for their ever-observant young daughter.
