Iconic performances from 80s luminaries Winona Ryder, Shannen Doherty and Christian Slater, and a cornucopia of gleefully nasty putdowns (“Lick it up baby. Lick. It. Up.”) mask an earnest plea for empathy and kindess at the center of HEATHERS’ black heart.

screenings.title: Out of the Blue
screenings.description: Dennis Hopper’s hurricane-force domestic tragedy is the ’80s answer to EASY RIDER, following troubled youth subculture to its frightening, screaming, self-annihilating extreme. Just out of prison for drunk-driving his truck into a school bus, delinquent dad Don (Dennis Hopper) returns home to the planet’s most messed up family: heroin-addict wife Kathy (Sharon Farrell) and self-destructive, Elvis Presley– and Sid Vicious–obsessed rebel-punk daughter Cebe (Linda Manz), whose mantra is “disco sucks, kill all hippies.” Driven by the teenage Manz’s stunningly raw performance, OUT OF THE BLUE has lost none of the furiously nihilistic power that shocked audiences upon its premiere.

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: The Oldest Person in the World
screenings.description: THE OLDEST PERSON IN THE WORLD is a decade-long odyssey chronicling the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. As the title inevitably passes from one supercentenarian to the next, acclaimed filmmaker Sam Green traverses the globe to meet each new record holder, his personal fascination with what the title means becoming entangled with events and milestones in his own life. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a poignant meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.

screenings.title: Tony
screenings.description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles in the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

screenings.title: The Dark Knight
screenings.description: The city of Chicago plays an oppressively glum Gotham in Nolan, Christian Bale, and Gary Oldman’s second Batman outing, a film of Langian architectural oppression that pits Bruce Wayne’s alter ego against Heath Ledger’s anarchic Clown Prince of Crime, with Oldman’s Commissioner Gordon the voice of law-and-order in an increasingly Bedlam-like city. Though Oldman may be known for his chameleonic transformations as an actor and his ability to comfortably occupy the skin of vastly different characters, he would in interviews cite Gordon as the character he’d played who is closest to himself: “A good sense of right and wrong… Family man. Just a regular geezer.”

screenings.title: Barbara Hammer: Embodied Histories
screenings.description: Research, recovery, and truth-telling become inseparable in Barbara Hammer’s radical, personal, and political cinema. Barbara Hammer’s mid- to late-career work approaches filmmaking as a form of research, using her camera to recover hidden histories and challenge dominant narratives. Her documentaries and essay films foreground the experiences of marginalized communities, weaving together personal testimony, archival inquiry, and formal experimentation. She expands the act of looking into a political encounter, charged with startling intimacy and urgency, to create a cinema of solidarity. Total runtime: Approx. 85 min. The History of the World According to a Lesbian U.S., 1988 Approx. 16 min. Anchored by the musical stylings of the Sluts from Hell, a fictional 1950s lesbian cover band quartet, Hammer’s playful survey traces visible and coded references to women loving women across human history: the fossilized lovers of prehistoric times, Platonic philosophy, early expressions of lesbianism in publishing, the subtextual queerness of the Hays Code era, and the punk mod era. Sisters! U.S., 1973 Approx. 8 min. Sisters! begins with the narration: “I had a dream of women where men used to be: building, working, growing strong, building their bodies into strength for self-defense.” The film stands as a joyous, essential landmark of feminist and lesbian filmmaking, weaving together what may be the only surviving footage of the first Women’s International Day march in San Francisco with rare footage from the second National Lesbian Conference at UCLA where Audre Lorde and Kate Millett spoke. “It’s about women taking over the world: women driving trucks, changing Volkswagen engines, and leading the police in new revolutions! It also has footage of women topless, dancing, sweating—with babies on their shoulders!” – Barbara Hammer Snow Job: The Media Hysteria of AIDS U.S., 1986 Approx. 8 min. Created during a period when misinformation about AIDS was rampant in the United States, Snow Job: The Media Hysteria of AIDS assembles video and audio fragments alongside mid-1980s news headlines deconstructing how mainstream media portrayed AIDS, arguing that its distortions and misrepresentations functioned as a “snow job” that fueled greater homophobia, sexual discrimination, and repression of gay people. “I first heard of AIDS in 1985 when I was teaching at Columbia College in Chicago. I noticed the strange and inflammatory articles in the newspapers and I asked my students to collect hysteric headlines for me. And so I began my work on Snow Job. I examined the public ignorance, stigmatization, and just plain wrong attitudes towards this new illness.” – Barbara Hammer Still Point U.S., 1989 Approx. 9 min. A four-screen film that whirls around a point of center, Still Point depicts Hammer and her longtime partner Florrie Burke as a middle-class lesbian couple navigating a class-divided society. Juxtaposing tender images of the couple in nature against the harsher realities of the streets of New York, the film grapples with questions of privilege and asks how a same-sex couple occupies public space amid social disparity. “At the still point of the turning world, that's where the dance is,” wrote T.S. Eliot in “Burnt Norton,” the first poem of Four Quartets. Witness: Palestine U.S., 2012 Approx. 13 min. Witness: Palestine was first shown at MoMA PS1 in 2012, projected onto seven volunteers in white shirts and masks. The film documents portraits of Palestinians Hammer met as part of the queer activist delegation during the first LGBTQ Solidarity Tour, sharing personal accounts of life under Israeli occupation and dismantling media stereotypes that demonize Palestinian resistance. One by one, they recount loss and hardship—a man who lost his village at six, a sister whose brother was killed by a rubber bullet, a farmer barred from his land—urgent testimonies of a people enduring ongoing conflict and danger. A Horse Is Not a Metaphor U.S., 2008 Approx. 29 min. In Hammer’s deeply personal film, she confronts her stage 3 ovarian cancer diagnosis on her own terms, rejecting the battle language often attached to illness, claiming the identity of “thriver,” instead of “survivor.” A Horse Is Not a Metaphor moves between the confined, clinical reality of chemotherapy and open, sensory scenes of Hammer on horseback riding across the red-earth landscape of Georgia O’Keeffe’s Ghost Ranch in New Mexico, through the grassy foothills of Wyoming’s Big Horn mountains, and along wooded trails near Woodstock, New York. Composer Meredith Monk’s guttural, electronically inflected score threads through these contrasting worlds. Programmed by Andrea Torres Presented with support from The R.G. Rifkind Foundation Endowment for Queer Cinema and The Roy Lichtenstein Foundation Fund Images courtesy of the Estate of Barbara Hammer, New York and Electronic Arts Intermix (EAI), New York.

screenings.title: Hope
screenings.description: A mysterious creature wreaks havoc on a South Korean village in Na Hong-jin’s sci-fi thriller.

screenings.title: Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma in 35mm
screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is handed over to an enthusiastic young director (Hannah Einbinder, Hacks) for resurrection. But when she visits the original movie’s star (Gillian Anderson, The X-Files, Sex Education), a now-reclusive actress shrouded in mystery, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, and delirium.

screenings.title: Onslaught
screenings.description: When a rogue squad of genetically engineered super soldiers break loose in the desert, a badass Army sniper must unleash hell to protect her young daughter.

screenings.title: The Odyssey
screenings.description: Odysseus fights monsters and menaces as he returns with his soldiers from the Trojan War.

screenings.title: The Hang-up
screenings.description: From this familiar premise – the innocents unknowingly walking into a den of vice – Hayes crafts a powerful chamber piece that plays like Tennessee Williams dragged into a (literal) trash heap. Brash, abusive junkyard owner Harry (Paul Leder, giving a manic performance that must be seen to be believed) quickly tries to implicate Ben in his shady dealings, while Harry’s beautiful but broken kept woman Poochie (McClanahan) tries her best to shake the foundations of his middle-class morality. Meanwhile, Edna finds herself pursued by Harry’s disturbed employee Blowhard (King Moody), while tortured poet/car thief Floyd (Norman Hartweg) muses on Freud and Nietzsche.

screenings.title: Don't Move
screenings.description: An annual camping trip takes a horrifying turn when a church group mistakenly hikes into an unknown area of a remote forest and finds themselves hunted by a giant, terrifying creature.

screenings.title: Hedda Lettuce Presents: the Star (1952)
screenings.description: New York City’s Premiere Drag Queen Hedda Lettuce presents THE STAR, an interactive event the likes of Rocky Horror meets Mystery Science Theater with barbed wit. With comedy, and commentary, Hedda highlights the highs, lows, and absurdities of this classic film! Oscar-winning actress Margaret Elliot is well past her prime but refuses to retire from the acting business. Despite entreaties from both her daughter, Gretchen, and one-time professional colleague Jim Johannsen, Margaret remains convinced that she can regain her former glory. As she sets her sights on a coveted Hollywood role, Johannsen tries doggedly to get his unrequited love to see the folly of her ways.

screenings.title: Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger
screenings.description: OASIS: DON'T LOOK BACK IN ANGER charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s triumphant reunion tour, Oasis Live ‘25, one of the most anticipated rock ‘n’ roll comebacks of our time. The film is an unapologetically uplifting account of the biggest musical event of 2025, capturing the experience and emotions of the band and their fans across the world. The unique perspective includes rehearsal, backstage, and onstage access as well as the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over 20 years. Alongside the band’s sold-out world tour, the film also explores the profound emotional impact of this phenomenal global cultural moment and what their music means to audiences and generations worldwide.

screenings.title: The Uprising
screenings.description: Andrew Garfield stars as the leader of a ferocious rebellion against the tyranny of King Richard II. Set against the true events of the Uprising that helped inspire the legend of Robin Hood, he forms an army of the people to face the King’s might in a fight for justice.

screenings.title: The Work in Progress
screenings.description: If you were invited to sit at a table with someone you’ve never met before and answer handwritten questions from a wooden box about the state of America, would you run the other way? The Work in Progress invites strangers from across generations and geographies to engage in candid discussions about America’s ever-evolving democracy, identity, and definitions of community — and where the heck we go from here. Guided by questions posed by Executive Producer Robert Reich, participants sit down in a series of conversations with one another to explore the country they’re living in now and the one they still believe is possible.

screenings.title: American Doctor
screenings.language: English, Arabic, and Hebrew with English Subtitles
screenings.description: From Oscar®-nominated and Emmy® Award-winning filmmaker Poh Si Teng, American Doctor follows three American physicians— Palestinian, Jewish, and Zoroastrian—united by a single oath to save lives. After volunteering in besieged hospitals in Gaza, they return home determined to fight for the patients and colleagues they left behind, taking their battle from the front lines of war to the halls of Congress.

screenings.title: Virginia Woolf’s Night & Day
screenings.description: Based on Virginia Woolf’s funniest novel, Night & Day follows passionate astronomer Katherine Hilbery as she does everything she can to avoid romantic love and marriage. Her bold challenge to Edwardian patriarchy is set against the suffragette movement and advances in science and technology. Fun and contemporary in tone, a refreshing film that showcases an ensemble of humorous performances in 1910 London that is as relevant to today as it ever was: women balancing love with careers!

screenings.title: Wake in Fright
screenings.description: It’s the eve of the Christmas holiday, and polite, young middle-class schoolteacher John Grant (Gary Bond), tied to a position at a tiny township in the outback, is on his way to Sydney to see his girlfriend by way of a stopoff in the grubby mining burg Bundanyabba (“The Yabba” to locals) when he pops into the pub for a drink… Five days of debauchery with local degenerates Donald Pleasence and Chips Rafferty later, the fresh-faced Grant has been replaced by a desperate, unshaven, beer-and-booze-pickled maniac, acquainted with species of depravity he could scarcely have imagined a week ago, and with the barbaric rites of the bush. A furious fever dream from Canuck director Kotcheff, who knew a thing or two about chronic self-degradation as practiced in far-flung outposts of the British Commonwealth, and one of the greatest of Australian films.

screenings.title: The Virgin Suicides
screenings.description: The directorial debut of Sofia Coppola. This adaptation of Jeffrey Eugenides’ novel tells the story of the Lisbon sisters, five angst-ridden teens living under the tight control of their repressive parents in 1970s suburbia. The Virgin Suicides is Coppola’s first collaboration with her eventual muse Kirsten Dunst, who gives a heartbreaking performance full of burgeoning sexuality. Also starring Kathleen Turner, James Woods & Josh Hartnett, and featuring a dreamy, mood-setting soundtrack by Air.

screenings.title: Megalopolis
screenings.description: U.S., 2024 Written and directed by Francis Ford Coppola Starring Adam Driver, Giancarlo Esposito, Jon Voight, Shia Laboeuf, Laurence Fishburne, Aubrey Plaza Approx. 138 min. “MEGALOPOLIS is equal parts STAR WARS prequel and MAN WITH A MOVIE CAMERA (1929). It’s Dario Argento’s DRACULA 3D (2012) and it’s Fellini’s SATYRICON (1969). More than anything else, it’s SOUTHLAND TALES, Richard Kelly’s 2006 head-scratcher of a follow-up to DONNIE DARKO (2001), but with less of Philip K. Dick’s DNA and more of Ayn Rand’s. It exists in conversation with APOCALYPSE NOW (1979), and it ends with a revised version of the pledge of allegiance being recited by a chorus of children. It’s a challenge to discuss it without bringing up a laundry list of cinematic reference points because, in the cubist tradition, it seems to break apart and rearrange over 100 years of film history into something completely baffling and new.” – Chicago Reader

screenings.title: Choy: Namibia, Independence Now + Reorienting Afri
Hope
screenings.description: In the remote South Korea village of Hope Harbor, police chief Bum-seok (Hwang Jung- min) and officer Sung-ae (Hoyeon) are called to find a mysterious creature that has wreaked havoc on the village. In the nearby forest, a coterie of hunters, including Sung- ki (Zo In-Sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

screenings.title: Ec: Michael
screenings.description: Shot by the great German cinematographers Karl Freund and Rudolph Maté, MICHAEL concerns the unconsummated homosexual love between a painter and his manipulative, larcenous model. The Danish director Benjamin Christensen stars as artist Claude Zoret, modeled in part after Rodin, whose irrepressible love finds its most complete expression in his last painting.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Finding Emily
screenings.description: When a lovesick musician is given the wrong number for his dream girl, he teams up with a driven psychology student to find her. Together, they spark a hilarious campus-wide frenzy that tests their own hearts and ambitions along the way.

screenings.title: Mysterious Skin
screenings.description: Director’s Statement: “I’m SO excited about the glorious 4K restoration of MYSTERIOUS SKIN! When we made this little indie 20 years ago, we barely had enough money to finish it, let alone pay for a Digital Intermediate and the bells and whistles of a larger studio film. I would never drastically alter the film which has such an amazing and passionate following around the world. However, the incredible tools made possible by modern digital technology helped us polish and enhance the picture in a way that wasn’t possible in the early 00’s. MYSTERIOUS SKIN holds a special place in my heart and I can’t wait for audiences, present and future, to experience this new definitive version of it.”

screenings.title: Coyote vs Acme
screenings.description: Wile E. Coyote teams up with a struggling lawyer to sue the ACME Corporation in this romp.

screenings.title: Colony
screenings.description: Horror master Yeon Sang-ho’s (Train to Busan) new zombie thriller stars Gianna Jun as biology professor Se-jeong, who’s thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong along with a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. Also starring Koo Kyo-hawn.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: In 1977, PK, a 23-year-old Delhi street artist from a poor, ‘untouchable’ family, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile cross-continent mission - to find Lotta, the woman who had captured his heart. A love story like no other, THE CYCLE OF LOVE is an inspiring, heart-warming, epic true-life adventure about the search for self-belief and risking everything for what your heart tells you.

screenings.title: The Sun Never Sets
screenings.description: Free-spirited Wendy (Dakota Fanning) is at a crossroads in her relationship with older divorced dad Jack (Jake Johnson, New Girl) that is only further complicated when an old flame (Cory Michael Smith, Sentimental Value) re-enters her life. Set in perpetually sunny summertime Anchorage and featuring a career-best performance by Fanning, THE SUN NEVER SETS is a funny and endearing return to form for mumblecore auteur Joe Swanberg.

Rather than traditional narratives, Tchaicovsky’s feature animations build immersive, breathing worlds where archaic symbols meet digital technology. His pioneering works explore the intersections of technology, consciousness, and art. “Cyberscape” and “Caught Between Worlds” merge futuristic digital architecture, surreal non-linear landscapes, and deeply atmospheric soundscapes.

screenings.language: English and Hindi with English Subtitles
screenings.description: A routine school commute turns terrifying when a cable car’s wire snaps, leaving eight passengers — including six schoolboys — dangling 900 feet above a ravine in the remote Himalayan foothills. With no margin for error and a cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of rescuers must improvise under intense public scrutiny, racing against an invisible clock before disaster strikes live on television.

screenings.title: Jennifer's Body
screenings.description: High school besties Anita and Jennifer (Amanda Seyfried and Megan Fox) are all but inseparable—though “Needy” Anita is a mousy bookworm and Jennifer a lusted-after member of the color guard—but can their opposites-attract dynamic survive Jennifer’s transformation into a succubus with an insatiable appetite for the flesh of their male classmates? A celebration of the pleasures of camp, kink, and practical gore effects that moves at sleek screwball feed thanks to Diablo Cody’s rat-a-tat screenplay, Kusama’s brisk direction, and the on-a-dime comic timing of its leads. (Not to speak of the redoubtable Amy Sedaris, as Anita’s perpetually disheveled, out-to-lunch mother.)

screenings.title: Chungking Express
screenings.description: A hot-shot to the heart, pop masterpiece Chungking Express tells the stories of two lovelorn cops (Takeshi Kaneshiro and Tony Leung) and the women who baffle them (Brigitte Lin and Faye Wong, who contributes a Cantopop cover of The Cranberries’ “Dreams”), its bifurcated structure suggesting the A- and B-sides of a 45. Wong’s international breakthrough introduced new audiences to his rich, sensorial brand of filmmaking, inviting one to disappear into, sink into, live inside, a voluptuary world bigger and brighter than our own—but just as heartbreaking.

screenings.title: Oasis: Don't Look Back in Anger
screenings.description: OASIS: DON'T LOOK BACK IN ANGER charts Liam and Noel Gallagher’s triumphant reunion tour, Oasis Live ‘25, one of the most anticipated rock ‘n’ roll comebacks of our time. The film is an unapologetically uplifting account of the biggest musical event of 2025, capturing the experience and emotions of the band and their fans across the world. The unique perspective includes rehearsal, backstage, and onstage access as well as the first joint interviews with Noel and Liam in over 20 years. Alongside the band’s sold-out world tour, the film also explores the profound emotional impact of this phenomenal global cultural moment and what their music means to audiences and generations worldwide.

screenings.title: Tony
screenings.description: A 19-year-old Anthony Bourdain travels to Provincetown and stumbles in the chaotic world of a restaurant kitchen, setting off a summer that will shape the course of his life.

screenings.title: The Oldest Person in the World
screenings.description: THE OLDEST PERSON IN THE WORLD is a decade-long odyssey chronicling the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. As the title inevitably passes from one supercentenarian to the next, acclaimed filmmaker Sam Green traverses the globe to meet each new record holder, his personal fascination with what the title means becoming entangled with events and milestones in his own life. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a poignant meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.

screenings.title: Filipiñana
screenings.description: “A masterwork—which is all the more remarkable given that it’s the first feature by the Filipino director Rafael Manuel... The film performs a scalpel-sharp dissection of the [luxury tourism] industry, laying bare a mad microcosm of power relations—political, sexual, economic, familial, cultural, even linguistic—and the aesthetic of dominance that the resort, in Manuel’s discerning view, projects... Manuel’s approach to narrative is as original as his sense of cinematic form, and his gift for documentary-style observation is balanced by a refined sense of style.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker “Darkly comic, visually inventive... cinematically builds into a scathing account of inequality, showing how women like Isabel are condemned to work in a place whose atmosphere is closer to that of a colonial plantation than a cushy country club.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “An invigorating dose of arch formalism in a sea of mainstream sincerity, this is the kind of movie that asks for the viewer’s attention and patience—not because it is slow or oblique but because it’s built entirely out of details... the angle of a golf club can evoke suspense, a piece of fruit on the ground can feel like a tragedy, and a casual glance can take your breath away.” – Bilge Ebiri, Vulture “Manuel uses his fastidiously arranged tableaux to give a tension and dark sense of humor to his fiery vision of Filipino high society. Set in an eerily well-manicured golf course outside Manila, this deadpan drama, with the symmetrical style of a Wes Anderson movie, patiently snakes its way through the club’s inner workings.” – Beatrice Loayza, The New York Times ★★★★ “Brilliantly biting... In a year of several standout debuts, Manuel’s ranks among the most impressive. The microcosm he meticulously constructs makes for a rivetingly caustic indictment of his homeland.” – Carlos Aguilar, RogerEbert.com

screenings.title: Dementia 13: Director’s Cut
screenings.description: U.S./Ireland, 1963/2017 Written and directed by Francis Ford Coppola Starring William Campbell, Luana Anders, Bart Patton, Mary Mitchel, Patrick Magee Produced by Roger Corman Approx. 69 min. “Produced by Roger Corman, and evidently made under his presiding spirit, Coppola’s debut runs briskly through one of those family reunion plots in which the challenge is to guess which seemingly benign member of the family is the mad axe-murderer who’s steadily picking off the rest. The location (an Irish castle) is used imaginatively, the Gothic atmosphere is suitably potent, and there’s a wonderfully sharp cameo from Patrick Magee as the family doctor.” – Time Out

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

screenings.title: Late Fame
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “A loving and lovely sensibility runs through LATE FAME, a fond and wise understanding of why some people want to become artists without making much art and why other people quit making it altogether.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “[A] lovely and bittersweet drama... Dafoe has rarely been so tender, playing a man allowing himself to dream again for the first time in forever.” – Tim Grierson, A/V Club “Like a wonderful little poem... Samy Burch, who also wrote the astute Oscar®-nominated script for 2023’s MAY DECEMBER, has crafted another subtle but powerful work.” – Kyle Smith, The Wall Street Journal “Lyrical and enchanting... Dafoe’s performance is like a slowly unfolding wildflower.” – Owen Gleiberman, Variety “Willem Dafoe is low key and magnificent as a former poet seemingly rescued from obscurity... In a prolific career filled with complex and striking characters, the role of Ed Saxberger is a subdued but particularly rich one for Dafoe, himself a veteran of the downtown arts scene.” – Sheri Linden, The Hollywood Reporter “LATE FAME is a deliciously acidic examination of the thin line between creative aspiration and pretentious poseurdom.” – Wendy Ide, Screen International

screenings.title: The Conversation
screenings.description: “DEVASTATINGLY BRILLIANT.” – Tony Rayns, Time Out “A TRIUMPH… GRITTY, COMPLEX, IDIOSYNCRATIC.” – David Denby “A GRIPPING MASTERPIECE.” – Peter Bradshaw, The Guardian “An immaculate thriller, a study in paranoia and loneliness, partly inspired by Antonioni’s BLOW-UP, and released as the Watergate scandal was unfolding, [with] one of Gene Hackman’s greatest performances.” – Philip French, The Guardian “When it premiered, the movie’s technological tricks and sleek corporate backdrop evoked Watergate. Thanks to Walter Murch’s keen, intuitive sound montage and Hackman’s clammy, subtle performance, captures a more elusive and universal fear—that of losing the power to respond, emotionally and morally, to the evidence of one’s own senses.” – Michael Sragow, The New Yorker “Harry ranks with Willy Loman in DEATH OF A SALESMAN or the pathetic captives of the middle class in John Cassavetes’ FACES.” – Roger Ebert “Remarkably ambitious and serious—a Hitchcockian thriller, a first-rate psychological portrait of a distinctive modern villain, and a bitter attack on American business values… all in one movie.” – David Denby

screenings.title: Troy
screenings.description: Before The Odyssey there was The Iliad, and before Christopher Nolan’s sword-and-sandals smash there was Troy, Petersen’s rather free adaptation of Homer (with a smidge of Quintus Smyrnaeus’s Posthomerica for flavor.) Orlando Bloom’s Paris lures the lovely Helen (Dianne Kruger) away from her throne in Sparta to the city of Troy, and so launches a thousand ships from the Peloponnese hellbent on dragging her back, among those aboard the fabled warrior Achilles (Brad Pitt) and the cunning strategist Odysseus (Sean Bean), soon to test their mettle against Trojan champion Hector (Eric Bana) and his armies. A strapping slab of impassioned spectacle, opulent production design, and earnest romanticism which, though critically divisive on its initial release, has in recent months seen the ranks of its admirers swell.

screenings.title: Brazil
screenings.description: Ground into despairing dust by his routine as a low-level bureaucrat in an Orwellian near-future—drabulously conceived as a junk shop jumble by art directors Norman Garwood and Maggie Gray—Sam (Jonathan Pryce) takes flight only in his imagination, where he plays the winged savior to distressed damsel Kim Griest. A chance teleprinter error at work and a wrongful arrest, however, set Sam on a course for real adventure, one involving his dream girl’s truck-driving double, a suspected terrorist (Robert De Niro), a freakshow cocktail party, plastic surgery disasters, and much more outlandishness besides. “A melancholy, joke-ridden view of the horribleness of where we are now and the worst horribleness of where we’re heading… It’s like a stoned, slapstick 1984: a nightmare comedy in which the comedy is just an aspect of the nightmarishness.” —Pauline Kael, The New Yorker

Both prequel and sequel to the original, as Pacino’s Michael consolidates his empire after dabbling in Cuban futures and vets the family for weaklings, while Oscar®-winner Robert De Niro, as the young Godfather-to-be, takes on the bosses of turn-of-the-20th-century Little Italy. screenings.description: Dennis Hopper’s hurricane-force domestic tragedy is the ’80s answer to EASY RIDER, following troubled youth subculture to its frightening, screaming, self-annihilating extreme. Just out of prison for drunk-driving his truck into a school bus, delinquent dad Don (Dennis Hopper) returns home to the planet’s most messed up family: heroin-addict wife Kathy (Sharon Farrell) and self-destructive, Elvis Presley– and Sid Vicious–obsessed rebel-punk daughter Cebe (Linda Manz), whose mantra is “disco sucks, kill all hippies.” Driven by the teenage Manz’s stunningly raw performance, OUT OF THE BLUE has lost none of the furiously nihilistic power that shocked audiences upon its premiere.

screenings.title: Wives (Hustruer)
screenings.description: First conceived of as a femme rejoinder to Husbands—and, like John Cassavetes’ film, heavy on collaboration and improvisation—Wives introduces us to Heidrun, Kaja, and Mie (Frøydis Armand, Katja Medbøe, and Anne Marie Ottersen), three married former classmates approaching 30 who, reunited at a high school reunion, decide—with the help of plenty of booze—not to hurry back to the domestic drudgery that awaits at home, instead taking to the streets and saunas of Oslo, keeping up a jocular running conversation that encompasses sex, motherhood, nagging regrets, and the manifold complications of adult life. “A charmer… Bubble[s] with a spontaneous humor tinged with rue… An accumulation of revelations.” —The New York Times

screenings.title: Peking Opera Blues
screenings.description: Set in the newly established, vulnerable Republican China of 1913, Peking Opera Blues is a fizzily exuberant, chaotically colorful espionage thriller/screwball romance/slapstick social satire/costume drama pageant that bends genres and genders at will, wending together the stories of three irrepressible female protagonists—played by Sally Yeh, Brigitte Lin, and Cherie Chung, respectively here as a would-be star of the all-male Peking Opera stage, a warlord’s headstrong daughter, and a courtesan who’s copped a case of stolen jewels. Frenetic, filled with whiplash-inducing tonal shifts, frightfully enjoyable and, in the opinion of Quentin Tarantino, “one of the greatest films ever made.”

screenings.title: The Taking of Pelham One Two Three
screenings.description: Dir. Joseph Sargent. 1974, 104 mins. 35mm. With Walter Matthau, Robert Shaw, Martin Balsam, Hector Elizondo. One of the great New York movies, bar none, Joseph Sargent’s fleet, funny, and frightening subway hijacking tale is both a crackerjack thriller and a slice of life in the Big Apple smack dab in the mid-seventies. Just before leaving office, Mayor Lindsay gave permission for it to be filmed on location—mainly in the tunnel of the abandoned Court Street station in Brooklyn and outside the subway entrance on 28th Street and Park Avenue South. The mayor is a character, but the movie is stolen by Lower East Side born Walter Matthau’s jaundiced police inspector—right through to the delicious final freeze frame. screenings.description: After years of slapdash sequels and waning fandom, the Camp Miasma slasher franchise is due for resurrection. And one young director is more than up to the task. But when she visits the original’s star, a now-reclusive actress, the two women fall into a blood-soaked world of desire, fear, delirium — under threat from the spear-wielding Little Death.

screenings.description: The debut of animation studio Gainax (Neon Genesis Evangelion) and a seminal work of cel animation, Royal Space Force: The Wings of Honnêamise was envisioned as an outside art film, countering the conventions of anime with its with its conceptual, Promethean ambitions.

screenings.title: 9/11, Pgm 1: Reichstag 9/11 + Disintegration Loop 1.1
screenings.description: So asks the Artist, one of three intertwined paranoiacs in Roger Copeland’s sprawling post-9/11, DIY, Brechtian fever dream. Proposing a twist on the axiom that the urge to destroy is also a creative urge, Copeland’s film suggests that all creativity is paranoid, and all paranoia is creative. It depicts a world that exists in “a state of semiotic arousal, a horniness for meaning.” Taking place in October of 2001, the film cuts between the story of a young girl who thinks the father that walked out on her family might be among the unrecovered dead at Ground Zero; the self-proclaimed BioEvangelist, who, in between compulsively consuming media coverage of the attacks’ aftermath in his basement chemistry lab, plans his own epistolary reckoning; and the aforementioned Artist, who monologues (livestreams?) from his studio about the ways the “death artists” have put art on the defensive.

screenings.title: Ec: the Passion of Joan of Arc
screenings.description: (LA PASSION DE JEANNE D’ARC)Spiritual rapture and institutional hypocrisy are brought to stark, vivid life in one of the most transcendent achievements of the silent era. Chronicling the trial of Joan of Arc in the final hours leading up to her execution, Dreyer depicts her torment with startling immediacy, employing an array of techniques – including expressionistic lighting, interconnected sets, and painfully intimate close-ups – to immerse viewers in her subjective experience. Anchoring Dreyer’s audacious formal experimentation is a legendary performance by Renée Falconetti, whose haunted face channels both the agony and the ecstasy of martyrdom.“With THE PASSION OF JOAN OF ARC, there occurs a most striking change in both the film-maker’s style and his intensity of thematic concentration. A few potent shots in previous movies hardly promise the unique and brilliant imagery which here bursts forth frame after frame. […] The vision of JOAN is inspired or demoniac. Her passion is observed with clinical detail in the sharp-etched, stark compositions, many relentless close-ups. But this is also loving detail, for Joan is the first of Dreyer’s possessed, a lineage which may be traced through the victims of VAMPYR to Anne in DAY OF WRATH and Johannes in ORDET; characters who work out their passions throughout the process of their films with peculiar intensity and directness, so that identification with the director himself is implicit.” –Ken Kelman, FILM CULTURECLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: Don't Move
screenings.description: An annual camping trip takes a horrifying turn when a church group mistakenly hikes into an unknown area of a remote forest and finds themselves hunted by a giant, terrifying creature.

screenings.title: Barbara Forever
screenings.description: “A veritable goldmine of queer cinema history, and a film worthy of its peerless subject.” – Sam Bodrojan, IndieWire “A beautifully assembled introduction to Hammer’s adventurous life and work... the aesthetic is that of a dynamic collagist, piecing together films, interviews and audio recordings into a portrait of real depth and style.” – Zachary Barnes, The Wall Street Journal “Barbara Hammer was a bad-ass punk rocker... this film lays bare the essence of an icon.” – Todd Haynes “A fantastic new documentary from director Brydie O’Connor (and produced by Christine Vachon’s Killer Films and Kristen Stewart), aims to introduce the filmmaker to a wider audience with help from Hammer herself. The film is narrated with Hammer’s voice—pulled from decades of audio diaries—and features interviews with [Hammer’s partner Florrie] Burke as well as footage from Hammer’s massive personal archive, including previously unreleased material... The documentary clarifies just how radical Hammer’s work was, and how it inspired many of the queer artists and filmmakers who came after her.” – Rachel Handler, Vulture “A remarkable collaboration between queer filmmakers past and present, and a testament to the impact of trailblazing. It’s an exhibition that inspires a call to action. BARBARA FOREVER is a chance to learn the legacy of what its subject deemed the art of living, making, and dying.” – Peyton Robinson, RogerEbert.com “A pioneer of lesbian cinema gets a documentary worthy of her.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Remarkable... A hypnotic portrait of an artist who endeavored to capture the vast scale of queer life... [imbued] with rare intimacy and tenderness.” – Maxwell Rabb, Harper’s Bazaar

screenings.title: Apocalypse Now: 1979 Roadshow Version
screenings.description: U.S., 1979 Directed by Francis Ford Coppola Inspired by Joseph Conrad’s novel, Heart of Darkness Starring Marlon Brando, Martin Sheen, Robert Duvall, Dennis Hopper, Frederic Forrest, Laurence Fishburne WINNER Cannes Film Festival – Palme d’Or, 1979 WINNER Academy Awards® – Best Cinematography, Best Sound, 1980 Approx. 149 min. “Starts with what proves to be a nightmare: a stand of pale green palm trees, ominous air-beating chops, the fleeting blurs of attack helicopters, a sudden rush of flame engulfing the trees as, in magically perfect rhythm, Jim Morrison’s high, thin voice croons, ‘This is the end...’ Then the dreamer of this recurring vision appears mingled with his own demonic images, in a Saigon hotel room during the Vietnam war, drunk, stunned, virtually deranged—an American captain named Benjamin Willard (Martin Sheen). Soon afterwards, his superiors send him upriver to Cambodia on a secret mission to find and kill a Green Beret colonel, Walter Kurtz (Marlon Brando), who is rumoured to be running amok there with a private army of Montagnard tribesmen and renegade Americans.” – Sight and Sound Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: On a String
screenings.description: Isabel (Isabel Hagen) is a young, Juilliard-trained violist still living at home with her parents in the heart of New York City. She’s trying to make a living playing gigs with her friends but when her toxic ex- boyfriend reappears, who also happens to be the Philharmonic’s “newest, hottest cellist,” he informs her of a viola opening in the prestigious orchestra. Nothing can go wrong, right?

screenings.title: Don't Play with Fire
screenings.description: Tsui’s outraged and outrageous third feature is a raw, tormented howl of hopeless rebellion that follows a trio of endorphin-addicted, bomb-planting teen nihilists as they get themselves involved with Triad thugs, gun runners, and—most perilous of all—a young woman (Lin Chen-chi) with a penchant for torturing small animals. Shredded by Hong Kong censors who blanched at its bloody-mindedness and its employment of shocking images from the city’s 1967 riots, Don’t Play with Fire (aka Dangerous Encounters of the First Kind) can be seen in a new restoration supervised by the director himself. An open provocation to anarchic upheaval, the blistering heat of its anti-establishment rage undiminished through the years.

screenings.title: Office Space
screenings.description: A household name thanks to the runaway success of MTV’s Beavis and Butthead, Judge made the leap into live-action filmmaking with this cult comedy of white-collar alienation, inspired by his 1991 animated short. Cubicle jockey Peter (Ron Livingston) checks out of his soul-sucking job for good after an encounter with an “occupational hypnotherapist” gone awry, only to have his superiors, impressed by his new air of utter indifference, pelt him with promotion after promotion. A wryly wicked satire about corporate culture and its gangsta rap-loving discontents.

screenings.title: Serpent's Path
screenings.description: A grieving father and a mysterious psychiatrist embark on a ruthless quest for vengeance after his daughter is murdered. As they abduct and interrogate suspects across Paris, the line between justice and obsession begins to blur, revealing a web of corruption and hidden truths that threatens to consume them both.

screenings.title: Out of the Blue
screenings.description: Dennis Hopper’s hurricane-force domestic tragedy is the ’80s answer to EASY RIDER, following troubled youth subculture to its frightening, screaming, self-annihilating extreme. Just out of prison for drunk-driving his truck into a school bus, delinquent dad Don (Dennis Hopper) returns home to the planet’s most messed up family: heroin-addict wife Kathy (Sharon Farrell) and self-destructive, Elvis Presley– and Sid Vicious–obsessed rebel-punk daughter Cebe (Linda Manz), whose mantra is “disco sucks, kill all hippies.” Driven by the teenage Manz’s stunningly raw performance, OUT OF THE BLUE has lost none of the furiously nihilistic power that shocked audiences upon its premiere.

screenings.title: Night of the Living Dead
screenings.description: Shot outside of Pittsburgh at a fraction of the cost of a Hollywood feature by a band of filmmakers determined to make their mark, George A. Romero’s Night of the Living Dead is one of the great stories of independent cinema: a midnight hit turned box-office smash that became one of the most influential films of all time. A deceptively simple tale of a group of strangers trapped in a farmhouse who find themselves fending off a horde of flesh-eating ghouls newly arisen from their graves, Romero’s claustrophobic vision of a late-sixties America (literally) tearing itself apart rewrote the rules of the horror genre, combined gruesome gore with acute social commentary, and quietly broke ground by casting a black actor (Duane Jones) in the lead role.

In the nearby forest, a coterie of local hunters, including Sung-ki (ZoIn-sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

screenings.title: Megacities
screenings.description: A protege of fellow Austrian Ulrich Seidl, Glawogger was occasionally painted with the brush of “provocateur,” but his deep empathy, humor, and relentless curiosity guides his films even through the most challenging subject matter. His “Globalization Trilogy” is a triptych of documentaries loosely dealing with the effects of shifting economic markets and modernization on some of the world’s most disenfranchised workers — though Glawogger disliked the “Globalization” framing, eschewing academic detachment to emphasize his audience and subjects’ shared humanity. In each of these films, Glawogger avoids ethnographic trappings by placing his protagonists center stage, never trivializing or overtly romanticizing them even as they experience some of the harshest conditions imaginable.

screenings.title: Uncut Gems
screenings.description: Adam Sandler gives a career-best performance as Howard Ratner, a fast-talking jeweler in Manhattan’s Diamond District with a penchant for living on the edge and well beyond his means, in the Safdies’ hectic, often hilarious thriller, where a debt-saddled Howie makes a series of high-stakes parlay bets on Kevin Garnett’s performance in the 2012 NBA playoffs that could lead to the windfall of a lifetime—or the abrupt end of his gambling career. “It’s gritty, but in the ’80s sense of it—gritty, with a lot of light and contrast. I started being a cinematographer in the ’80s, so they went back to this period of time where we were after very strong, ink blacks, very long lenses, very contrast-y images, very harsh contours… It was completely unlike anything I’ve done. I would never have thought I would photograph one day a movie like this. But it ended up being my favorite work, probably.” —Darius Khondji

A sort-of sequel to Wong’s Days of Being Wild and In the Mood for Love, the ’60s-set 2046 revisits Tony Leung Chiu-wai’s Chow, now a suave science-fiction writer, to chronicle his various affairs with women (including Faye Wong, Zhang Ziyi, and Gong Li), acting as distractions now that his true love, Mrs. Chen (Maggie Cheung, seen in flashback), has disappeared. Intercutting scenes from Chow’s footloose life—several of these taking place on subsequent Christmas Eves—with scenes from his novel-in-progress, set in the titular year, it’s a film of voluptuous melancholy.

screenings.title: Manhunter: The Final Cut
screenings.description: A retired criminal profiler (William Petersen) reluctantly returns to the FBI to help track down a serial killer of families and is forced to consult an expert—the imprisoned Dr. Hannibal Lecktor (Brian Cox in a subtly chilling performance). The third feature written and directed by Michael Mann is a gripping adaptation of the first of Thomas Harris’s four novels featuring the iconic murderer Lecktor, and benefits from the filmmaker’s typically striking visuals as well as a top-notch supporting cast, including Tom Noonan as the hunted killer and three-time Oscar nominee Joan Allen as his blind love interest.

screenings.title: Sweet Trash
screenings.description: From this familiar premise – the innocents unknowingly walking into a den of vice – Hayes crafts a powerful chamber piece that plays like Tennessee Williams dragged into a (literal) trash heap. Brash, abusive junkyard owner Harry (Paul Leder, giving a manic performance that must be seen to be believed) quickly tries to implicate Ben in his shady dealings, while Harry’s beautiful but broken kept woman Poochie (McClanahan) tries her best to shake the foundations of his middle-class morality. Meanwhile, Edna finds herself pursued by Harry’s disturbed employee Blowhard (King Moody), while tortured poet/car thief Floyd (Norman Hartweg) muses on Freud and Nietzsche.

screenings.description: The story of neo-cool Enid (Thora Birch) and Rebecca (Scarlett Johansson) who, faced with graduation from high school, take a hard look at the world they wryly observe and decide what they really want. When Enid takes an interest in the offbeat Seymour (Steve Buscemi) and Rebecca focuses her attention on their mutual romantic fixation Josh (Brad Renfro), the girls’ friendship is forever changed.

screenings.description: Lawrence Kasdan’s tramped up and ruthless remix of Double Indemnity, sees a Florida heat-wave fry the brain of a dopey two-bit lawyer who falls into the trap of a bored and wealthy woman just out to pass the time while her husband’s out of town with a bit of a steamy affair. As the clothes shed and the days pass, a plot hatches to kill her husband and make off with his mountain of money. Dopey lawyer being what he is, goes for it; but one can hardly blame him, it’s for Kathleen Turner, after all.

screenings.director: Hou Hsiao-hsien, Tseng Chuang-hsiang, Wan Jen
screenings.description: A foundational text of the Taiwanese New Wave, omnibus triptych The Sandwich Man represented a clean break from the cloying sentimentality of most of the country’s studio product, with director’s Hou, Wan, and Tseng each adapting stories from a collection by Huang Chung-ming and addressing, with bracing directness, the harsh realities of contemporary urban life. Hou bats leadoff with the devastating namesake segment, about a man eking out a living as a human advertising board; Tseng’s Vickie’s Hat offers a cautionary tale about the perils of modern convenience, namely imported Japanese pressure cookers; Wan’s The Taste of Apples acquaints us with a family in the Taipei City slums whose only hope for a glimpse of the good life is a bed in the American Navy hospital.

screenings.title: Stealing Beauty
screenings.description: After the death of her poet mother, 19-year-old American Lucy (Liv Tyler) travels to a Tuscan villa near Siena owned by family friends in hopes of exploring her family’s history and reuniting with her first kiss, though soon finds herself contending with a crowded field of would-be suitors. Working in his native Italy for the first time in 15 years, and in his only collaboration with DP Darius Khondji, Bertolucci creates a film of warm, mellow light; lyrical grace notes; and exquisite performances from Tyler, Joseph Fiennes, Jeremy Irons, Rachel Weisz, and others.

screenings.title: Junk Dump Film Festival 2026: Day One
screenings.description: Museum of the Moving Image and Junk Dump Magazine will present Junk Dump’s sixth annual short film festival. Junk Dump Magazine is a not-for-profit arts organization that produces a semi-annual print publication and events like Junk Dump Film Festival, which highlights emerging and underrepresented filmmakers working at the intersection of video art and storytelling. The festival presents a curated program of narrative, animated, and experimental short films made by artists using unique processes to tell singular and engaging stories. This year’s selection was guest judged and curated by two New York–based filmmakers. Caroline Mariko Stucky (she/they) is an award-winning Swiss-Japanese cinematographer, and the founder and creative director of CM8 Productions, a film and video production company specializing in independent films, music videos, and fashion films. Sidney Rose White is a Texas-born actress, model, and illustrator based in New York City. She can be seen in Wes and Kyra, HULU’s Red Is the Color of Beauty, Awesome, and Schon! Magazine’s Sheltering with You. Day One programming will include a selection of seven narrative and documentary shorts. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with the filmmakers. Screening run time approx. 100 min. Featuring: Vowels Dir. Rafael De Leon. 2025, 5 mins. U.S. Ava needs to record a self-tape, but her speech impediment keeps getting in the way. SHORT KING Dir. Yoni Azulay. 2026, 10 mins. U.S. An insecure, status-obsessed man spirals into obsession and sabotage after a charming guest calls him “short” at his surprise birthday party. The Lion of Teranga Dir. Marcus Quinn. 2025, 14 mins. U.S. While chasing a championship with his team, a young basketball player is drawn into an unsettling incident with his coach, threatening his friendship with his closest teammate. Sweet Tooth Dir. Benji Tucker. 2025, 13 mins. U.S. As Doe Town gears up for its 55th Annual Smile Contest, undefeated champion Bucky Bantershire begins to unravel when his long-suppressed Sweet Tooth resurfaces, singing, dancing, and dragging him into sugary chaos. Why Can’t We All Get Along? Dir. Nicholas Liam Dinner. 2025, 14 mins. U.S. Two drifting friends recovering from substance abuse reconnect with their mutual ex on the eve of their 5-year high school reunion. Bad habits and emotional manipulation test their relationship as the boys ask the question: are we meant to be friends? Purely Patricia Dir. Jasper Soloff. 2026, 13 mins. U.S. This intimate short documentary follows New York style icon Patricia Fox, a woman who treats every day as an occasion to dress up. Known for her exuberant fashion and joyful presence, Patricia embodies a life lived in color and self-expression. But beneath the twirls and textures lies a quieter reckoning with time. Always Dreaming Dir. Jasmine Garcia Delossantos. 2025, 7 mins. U.S. A housekeeper shares her dreams and ambitions as her daily work routine consists of cleaning hotel rooms during Oregon’s busiest tourist season. Hometown Famous Dir. Vivian Wolfson and Asher Kaye. 2026, 20 min. U.S. Hometown Famous follows the tumultuous 30-year-long history of northeast Ohio’s premier Fleetwood Mac tribute band, exploring the significance of tribute bands in modern American music culture. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

Just out of prison for drunk-driving his truck into a school bus, delinquent dad Don (Dennis Hopper) returns home to the planet’s most messed up family: heroin-addict wife Kathy (Sharon Farrell) and self-destructive, Elvis Presley– and Sid Vicious–obsessed rebel-punk daughter Cebe (Linda Manz), whose mantra is “disco sucks, kill all hippies.” Driven by the teenage Manz’s stunningly raw performance, OUT OF THE BLUE has lost none of the furiously nihilistic power that shocked audiences upon its premiere.

Equal parts 2001: A Space Odyssey, Rosemary’s Baby, and Electric House, and showcasing an exquisite cybernetic psych-out sequence aided by visionary artist Jordan Belson and visual effects wizard Ron Hays, this post-humanist thriller unveils supercomputer Proteus IV: the latest invention of corporate monolith ICON that can cure leukemia, develop mining techniques, and ruminate on Buddhism with equal facility. When threatened, the hubristic machine seeks self-preservation by infiltrating the high-tech home of ICON’s lead scientist, trapping his wife and preparing her to propagate a new hybrid life form with his eponymous synthetic spermatozoa. Wiseman’s New York: Ex-Libris: The New York Public Library
screenings.description: Introduced by critic and guest programmer Genevieve Yue Dir. Frederick Wiseman. 2017. 197 mins. Digital projection. Fifty years and 42 documentaries into his legendary career, Frederick Wiseman brings his incisive vision to one of the world’s greatest institutions of learning, capturing the vast programmatic scope of the New York Public Library. From the storied Fifth Avenue main branch to the Schomburg Center in Harlem to numerous of the 92 branches across Manhattan, the Bronx, and Staten Island, Wiseman finds a staff grappling with what a 21st–century library should and could be, guests from Patti Smith to Ta-Nehisi Coates wrestling with ideas and history, and New Yorkers of all races and classes coming together to learn, engage, and access resources, exemplifying the value of community. This screening is presented in collaboration with UnionDocs’ special inter-borough series Wiseman’s New York. Over the course of his six-decade career, the late, great documentarian returned to New York more than any single location, making nine films in the city, from Hospital (1970) and Welfare (1975) toIn Jackson Heights (2015) and Ex-Libris (2017). screenings.description: 35mm Import. An erotic thriller starring an unhinged Christopher Walken alongside a seductive Joan Chen, Wild Side indulges in a rapacious world of power, money and sex. Screening in its breathtaking Director’s Cut—lost for decades and assembled after Cammell (Performance) took his own life when the film was recut. This revelatory edit will be shown on one of only two prints ever made.

screenings.title: Dust in the Wind
screenings.description: Young lovers Wan and Huen, fresh out of junior high school in the remote, mountainous mining town where they were raised, look forward to a bright future together in their new home of Taipei—only to face first the grim reality of urban life there, then a three-year separation, after Wan is drafted into the Republic of China Army, which ultimately proves fatal to their affections. Based on the personal experiences of frequent Hou co-screenwriter Wu Nien-jen, the poignant, plangent Dust in the Wind has emerged as a popular favorite among Hou’s films, his first collaboration with composer Chen Ming-chang and actor Li Tian-lu, which also features some of Mark Lee Ping-bing’s most hypnotically beautiful tracking shots.

screenings.title: I Hired a Contract Killer
screenings.description: Freshly unemployed after 15 years at the same civil service post, newly turned 50, and too frightened to put himself out of his misery by his own hand, Jean-Pierre Léaud, a Frenchman living in London, decides to hire a hitman to do the dirty work for him—but this final solution runs into a wrinkle when he rediscovers his will to carry on after falling madly in love, leaving him to scramble to cancel the contract. A deadpan hilarious and disarmingly poignant comedy from Finland's eminent master of the genre, giving Léaud perhaps his finest English-speaking role.

screenings.title: I Walked with a Zombie
screenings.description: She’s alive…yet dead! She’s dead…yet alive! Betsy Connell believed she had seen strange behavior from her patients, but nothing in her training and experience has prepared her for the voodoo, horror and walking undead of a Caribbean island in visionary director Jacques Tourneur’s I Walked with a Zombie. Who said the dead don’t walk? Connell (Frances Dee) travels to the Caribbean to care for the comatose wife of plantation owner Paul Holland (Tom Conway). But as Connell starts to fall in love with Holland, she gradually realizes that her patient is not comatose: She neither lives nor dies, existing as something not quite human and not quiet demon.

Cubicle jockey Peter (Ron Livingston) checks out of his soul-sucking job for good after an encounter with an “occupational hypnotherapist” gone awry, only to have his superiors, impressed by his new air of utter indifference, pelt him with promotion after promotion. screenings.title: Rebels of the Neon God
screenings.description: Tsai’s first theatrically released film isn’t as pared down in its approach as some of his later works—it even has a rather catchy synth theme song!—but in most respects it’s pure Tsai, a film about urban loners and the city’s (largely unfulfilled) promises of connection and sexual intimacy. Lee Kang-sheng, Tsai’s acteur fétiche, stars as a teenaged Taipei arcade rat who develops an obsession with a young petty hoodlum (Chen Chao-jung) that’s a tangle of vengeful wrath and repressed lust. An extraordinary debut, in which aspects of all its maker’s films to come are visible.

screenings.title: Junk Dump Film Festival 2026: Day Two
screenings.description: Museum of the Moving Image and Junk Dump Magazine will present Junk Dump’s sixth annual short film festival. Junk Dump Magazine is a not-for-profit arts organization that produces a semi-annual print publication and events like Junk Dump Film Festival, which highlights emerging and underrepresented filmmakers working at the intersection of video art and storytelling. The festival presents a curated program of narrative, animated, and experimental short films made by artists using unique processes to tell singular and engaging stories. This year’s selection was guest judged and curated by two New York–based filmmakers. Caroline Mariko Stucky (she/they) is an award-winning Swiss-Japanese cinematographer, and the founder and creative director of CM8 Productions, a film and video production company specializing in independent films, music videos, and fashion films. Sidney Rose White is a Texas-born actress, model, and illustrator based in New York City. She can be seen in Wes and Kyra, HULU’s Red Is the Color of Beauty, Awesome, and Schon! Magazine’s Sheltering with You. Day Two programming will include a selection of nine experimental and animated shorts. The screening will be followed by a Q&A with the filmmakers. Screening run time approx. 80 mins. Featuring: Through the Fog Dir. William Bishop. 2026, 8 mins. U.S. Littlefish Dir. Yuhyeon Byun. 2025, 9 mins. Czechia/U.S. A young woman relies on a magical rybička with the ability to answer any question to navigate her unresolved feelings for a man she once shared an intense connection with. The Frame Dir. Caroline Johnson. 2025, 3 mins. U.S. How do you depict the undepictable? The frame: a container. a boundary. a moment. Is it a unit of time or space—or of both? The existence of a frame necessarily implies something within, and consequently something outside. The Frame is an exploration of spatial and temporal boundaries through the lens of paintings of the late Renaissance, when artists wrestled with how to portray that which, by definition, cannot be portrayed. Midnight Service Dir. Kaylee Smith. 2025, 07 mins. U.S. On an evening exploring the liminal spaces of small-town Heber City, Utah, a girl lurks in the shadows, confronting her estranged contention with the religious culture. Sunset Smudge Dir. Jesse LoCascio. 2025, 8 mins. U.S., Amidst a sweltering heat wave, a young woman grapples with the slow decay and inevitable demise of her once beautiful surroundings. Let us see you again – تاني نش و ف ك خلينا Dir Lobna Morsi and Herlinde Raeman. 2026, 18 mins. Belgium. Let Us See You Again explores homecoming not as a destination, but as a journey between memory and present reality, belonging and transition. It is a tender, intergenerational epic about resilience, negotiation, and the continuous act of becoming. What do you see and hear in the quiet margins of a space when home is shaped by distance or time? How do you make room for a retour that is not merely a welcome, but also a farewell? Beneath the Concrete, the Forest Dir. Lev Omelchenko. 2026, 12 mins U.S. A short experimental documentary that takes us inside an ongoing struggle in the city of Atlanta, GA, between two sides to determine the future of Weelaunee, the biggest contiguous urban forest in the country. Atrium, or The Girl Who Painted Hats and Met the Sky Dir. Zoe Napurano. 2026, 06 mins. U.S. A young hat painter dreams of a strange lady. Why Look at Animals Dir. Maya Perry. 2019, 8 mins. U.S. Lo Sguardo (The Gaze) Dir. Gloria Zingales. 2024, 10 mins. U.S. When the news of an encroaching fire and an unsettling onlooker interrupt a night amongst friends, Sole—a young Italian woman—must return home alone. On her journey, Sole faces dangers that blur the line between reality and her own paranoia. Lo Sguardo is a short giallo thriller about the male gaze and its psychological effects on women. screenings.description: Dir. Claire Simon. 2023, 168 mins. France. DCP. Master documentary filmmaker Simon (The Grocer’s Son, the Mayor, the Village and the World and Young Solitude) trains her camera on a gynecological ward in a public hospital in Paris. Over the course of many months of filming, and through interactions with a multitude of women, Simon captures a spectrum of fears, desires, and struggles, and a representation of women at all stages of life. screenings.title: Night of the Living Dead
screenings.description: Shot outside of Pittsburgh at a fraction of the cost of a Hollywood feature by a band of filmmakers determined to make their mark, George A. Romero’s Night of the Living Dead is one of the great stories of independent cinema: a midnight hit turned box-office smash that became one of the most influential films of all time. A deceptively simple tale of a group of strangers trapped in a farmhouse who find themselves fending off a horde of flesh-eating ghouls newly arisen from their graves, Romero’s claustrophobic vision of a late-sixties America (literally) tearing itself apart rewrote the rules of the horror genre, combined gruesome gore with acute social commentary, and quietly broke ground by casting a black actor (Duane Jones) in the lead role.

screenings.director: Maria Jose Cuevas, Benjamin H. Stavillo
screenings.description: Mexico’s most iconic concert comes to U.S. theaters on September 15th, celebrating Mexican Independence Day and commemorating the 10th anniversary of Juan Gabriel’s passing. Experience his legendary first performance at Mexico City’s “Palacio de Bellas Artes” in 1990–a landmark event that forever transformed Mexican music. More than three decades later, this historic concert returns in a special theatrical release with newly restored picture and sound, plus an exclusive new opening featuring never-before-seen rehearsal footage from Juan Gabriel’s personal archive that offers a unique glimpse into the making of this unforgettable night. Every song, every standing ovation, and every iconic moment has been revitalized, allowing longtime fans and new audiences to experience this extraordinary performance like never before. Celebrate the timeless legacy of Juan Gabriel on the big screen in this once-in-a-generation cinematic event.

screenings.title: I Walked with a Zombie
screenings.description: She’s alive…yet dead! She’s dead…yet alive! Betsy Connell believed she had seen strange behavior from her patients, but nothing in her training and experience has prepared her for the voodoo, horror and walking undead of a Caribbean island in visionary director Jacques Tourneur’s I Walked with a Zombie. Who said the dead don’t walk? Connell (Frances Dee) travels to the Caribbean to care for the comatose wife of plantation owner Paul Holland (Tom Conway). But as Connell starts to fall in love with Holland, she gradually realizes that her patient is not comatose: She neither lives nor dies, existing as something not quite human and not quiet demon.

Identical twin sisters Margaret (Bette Davis) and Edith Philips (also Davis) haven't spoken in nearly 20 years, ever since Margaret hoodwinked the man Edith loved into marrying her instead. When Margaret's husband dies, Edith reunites with her twin -- but only to seek revenge. Killing her sister and stealing her identity, Edith has everyone convinced she's really Margaret. But when she encounters Margaret's lover, Tony (Peter Lawford), Edith uncovers a shocking secret that threatens her plans.

screenings.description: THE OLDEST PERSON IN THE WORLD is a decade-long odyssey chronicling the ever-changing record holders of the title of oldest person alive. As the title inevitably passes from one supercentenarian to the next, acclaimed filmmaker Sam Green traverses the globe to meet each new record holder, his personal fascination with what the title means becoming entangled with events and milestones in his own life. What begins as a portrait of longevity becomes a poignant meditation on the passage of time, the randomness of fate and the joy and profound human experience of being alive.

screenings.title: Hope

In the nearby forest, a coterie of local hunters, including Sung-ki (ZoIn-sung) set out to track the beast and find themselves hunted instead. But all is not as it seems, and perceptions can be misleading. What begins as ignorance plants the seed of disaster, escalating through human conflict into a tragedy of cosmic proportions.

screenings.title: Yi Yi
screenings.description: The last work of a master filmmaker who died far too young, the gentle, restrained, and terribly humane Yi Yi observes the interplay between three generations of an upper middle-class Taipei family. Comic when dealing in the foibles of its excellent ensemble cast and the mores of the urban bourgeoise, yet also possessed throughout by an air of unmistakable melancholy and lingering regret at missed opportunities, this feeling made all the deeper when one considers the great films Yang might still have produced. A work of epic length that avoids even a hint of bombast, dedicated instead to working its way into the hidden, niche spaces of everyday people’s emotional lives, it’s a film as rich and as sad as life itself.

screenings.description: Don’t cry for her, Argentina—after years of dauntless campaigning, Madonna landed the coveted role of actress-cum-First Lady Eva Perón in this lavish, costume-change-a-minute adaptation of Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber’s 1978 stage musical, featuring Jonathan Pryce as the statesman who shares his power and his bed with Eva, and Antonio Banderas as narrator of her meteoric rise and tragic end. “Evita is actually a very visual movie, and Alan Parker is probably one of the most exciting and visual directors I have ever worked with… He wanted to make the film look very real, almost like a newsreel, but also very glamorous at the same time… There were certain scenes where we had up to 4,000 or 5,000 extras, because Alan didn’t want to use any special effects—he wanted it all to be in front of the lens.” —Darius Khondji

screenings.description: Dir. Robert Berry. 1963, 71 mins. U.S. DCP. With Robert Berry, Pauline Elliott. A frustrated author is plagued by recurring nightmares centered around a haunted house in House of Dreams, where the boundaries of reality do not blur because they never existed in the first place. Shot on gritty 16mm film stock in Indiana and never legitimately distributed, House of Dreams is a hidden chapter of mid-century, avant garde horror from director/star Robert Berry that is as haunting as it is sincere. screenings.title: Climate Film Festival Opening Night: House of Fish
screenings.description: Followed by a discussion with director Santiago Burin des Roziers and reception House of Fish Dir. Santiago Burin des Roziers. 2026, 85 mins. In Italian with English subtitles. At the crossroads of art, activism, and the ocean lies the extraordinary story of Paolo Fanciulli, a humble Italian fisherman with a revolutionary vision. After witnessing decades of destruction caused by illegal bottom trawling, Paolo devised a bold solution: an underwater museum of monumental marble sculptures that protect the seabed by preventing trawling while standing as powerful symbols of hope and resistance. House of Fish follows his remarkable journey, blending intimate personal storytelling with a natural history perspective on the fragile Mediterranean ecosystem. Through breathtaking underwater cinematography, the film reveals the devastating impact of industrial fishing on endangered marine life and vital habitats, including Posidonia oceanica, a seagrass essential to biodiversity and carbon capture. More than a conservation documentary, House of Fish is a cinematic celebration of courage, creativity, and community, inspiring audiences to reconnect with the ocean and recognize that one person’s vision can help transform the future of our seas. East Coast premiere. Followed by a reception from 9:00-11:00 p.m. Tickets: $20 / 25% discount for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order Tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission. About the Climate Film Festival: The Climate Film Festival (CFF) is both an annual film festival held in New York City during Climate Week NYC and a year-round nonprofit cultural organization. Founded in 2023, CFF harnesses the power of motion pictures to reshape the conversation around climate change, making urgent issues accessible, engaging, and action-oriented through the cinematic lens. Each year, the festival presents a curated selection of scripted, documentary, feature, short, episodic, and experimental works, alongside filmmaker conversations, educational programming, and the Narrative Change Summit. Committed to formal innovation, environmental justice, and community engagement, CFF amplifies bold voices and inspiring films that reframe the conversation around climate action. Special Guest: Santiago Burin des Roziers was born in Buenos Aires, Argentina and moved to London to pursue a career in filmmaking. Not long after film school, he started directing. His projects have taken him around the globe, to over 30 countries. He has made films for the BBC, Channel 4 and VICE, as well as for brands such as Coca– Cola, Sony, Red Bull, and Adidas.
